catalog.name: Taxes calculations
catalog.description: Every formula, algorithm, rounding rule and worked example of the tax domain, in a structured form a rebuild can test against: the rounding primitives and their tie-breaking, the flattening, ordering and batching of taxes, the amount of each computation kind, the propagation of one tax's amount into another tax's base, the single-line computation and its two currencies, the six document-wide rounding passes and the two rounding methods, the derivation of the accounting data and the report tags, the manual amounts and computation keys, the totals block with its subtotal cascade and its two cash rounding strategies, the fiscal position mapping and unit price adaptation, the cash basis percentages and shares, the withholding amounts, the document-level helpers, the whole tax identification number pipeline with its shared primitives and one record per country check, and the reconstruction of the base-to-tax mapping from posted journal items.
catalog.authored_from: docs/domains/taxes/calculations.md, with the ledger effects of docs/domains/taxes/accounting-effects.md and the rule sections of docs/domains/taxes/business-rules.md

records.name: Reading a supplied price under the special mode saying it excludes every tax
records.purpose: The first of the two overrides of what a supplied price means: the caller states that the price carries no tax at all, so every tax, including one flagged price-included, is added on top of it.

operands.name: supplied unit price
operands.source: the caller
operands.constraints: understood as the amount without any tax

operands.name: own price-inclusion flag of each tax
operands.source: each tax
operands.constraints: overridden for the computation but still read by the propagation table

operands.name: rate of each tax
operands.source: each tax
operands.constraints: none

preconditions.condition: The base line carries the special mode saying the price excludes every tax.
preconditions.otherwise: The price means what the taxes say, or the other special mode applies.

preconditions.condition: The price is not already rounded and the document-wide rounding method is round per tax.
preconditions.otherwise: Symmetry with the other special mode is not guaranteed and the two directions can differ by one unit of the last decimal place.

procedure: Force the effective price-inclusion flag of every tax to false, whatever the tax's own flag says, except for a tax with a negative distribution factor, which is price-excluded in any case.
Take the supplied price as the raw base, without extracting anything from it.
Add every tax on top of that base by the formula of its own computation kind.

Choose the row of the propagation table by each tax's own configured price-inclusion flag, not by the effective flag this mode forces: a price-included tax that affects the base adds its amount back to every later tax that accepts being affected, because the caller already handed a price with the included taxes removed.
records.formula: effective price inclusion of every tax = false ; raw_base = quantity × supplied unit price ; total_excluded = raw_base ; total_included = raw_base + sum of every tax amount ; supplying a price of 100 with a price-included tax of 21 percent under this mode gives the same result as supplying 121 with no mode

rounding.what: The raw base and every tax amount, as in the ordinary computation.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the line currency and of the company currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero.
rounding.step: Immediately under the round-per-line method; in the document-wide passes under the round-per-tax method.

result.name: the untaxed total and the total with taxes of the line
result.unit_or_currency: the line currency and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Held on the tax details block and shown in the totals block.

edge_cases.case: A tax has a negative distribution factor.
edge_cases.outcome: Its effective flag is false in any case, because a reverse-charge tax is always treated as price-excluded.

edge_cases.case: The price was pre-rounded, or the document-wide method is round per line.
edge_cases.outcome: The result may differ from the equivalent computation under the other mode by one unit of the last decimal place.

edge_cases.case: A price-included tax that affects the base is evaluated under this mode.
edge_cases.outcome: Its amount is added back to every later tax that accepts being affected, so that the base those taxes are meant to be charged on is reconstructed.

worked_examples.description: The equivalence the document states

expected_outputs.equivalent_computation: supplying one hundred twenty-one with no special mode

worked_examples.narrative: The twenty-one percent tax is flagged price-included, but the mode forces it on top of the price: the untaxed total is one hundred, the tax twenty-one and the total with taxes one hundred twenty-one, which is exactly what supplying one hundred twenty-one with no mode gives.

records.name: Reading a supplied price under the special mode saying it includes every tax
records.purpose: The second of the two overrides: the caller states that the price already carries every tax, so every tax, including one flagged price-excluded, is extracted from it.

operands.name: supplied unit price
operands.source: the caller
operands.constraints: understood as the amount with all taxes

operands.name: own price-inclusion flag of each tax
operands.source: each tax
operands.constraints: overridden for the computation but still read by the propagation table

operands.name: rate of each tax
operands.source: each tax
operands.constraints: none

preconditions.condition: The base line carries the special mode saying the price includes every tax.
preconditions.otherwise: The price means what the taxes say, or the other special mode applies.

preconditions.condition: The price is not already rounded and the document-wide rounding method is round per tax.
preconditions.otherwise: Symmetry with the other special mode is not guaranteed and the two directions can differ by one unit of the last decimal place.

procedure: Force the effective price-inclusion flag of every tax to true, whatever the tax's own flag says, except for a tax with a negative distribution factor, which stays price-excluded.
Take the supplied price as the raw base and extract every tax from it by the formula of its own computation kind.
Subtract the batch total from the reported base of each tax in the base pass, because the effective flag is true and the mode is the including one.

Choose the row of the propagation table by each tax's own configured price-inclusion flag: a price-excluded tax that affects the base has its amount removed only from the earlier taxes, because the later ones already contain it by construction, while one that does not affect the base is removed from everybody's base.
records.formula: effective price inclusion of every tax = true ; raw_base = quantity × supplied unit price ; base of a tax = raw_base + extra_base_for_base − batch_total ; total_excluded = the base of the first entry ; total_included = total_excluded + sum of every tax amount ; supplying a price of 121 with a price-excluded tax of 21 percent under this mode gives the same result as supplying 100 with no mode

rounding.what: The raw base and every tax amount, as in the ordinary computation.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the line currency and of the company currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero.
rounding.step: Immediately under the round-per-line method; in the document-wide passes under the round-per-tax method.

result.name: the untaxed total and the total with taxes of the line
result.unit_or_currency: the line currency and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Held on the tax details block and shown in the totals block.

edge_cases.case: A tax has a negative distribution factor.
edge_cases.outcome: Its effective flag stays false, so a reverse-charge tax is not extracted from the price even under this mode.

edge_cases.case: The price was pre-rounded, or the document-wide method is round per line.
edge_cases.outcome: The result may differ from the equivalent computation under the other mode by one unit of the last decimal place.

edge_cases.case: A price-excluded tax that affects the base is evaluated under this mode.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the earlier taxes have its amount removed, because the later taxes already contain it by construction.

worked_examples.description: The equivalence the document states

expected_outputs.equivalent_computation: supplying one hundred with no special mode

worked_examples.narrative: The twenty-one percent tax is flagged price-excluded, but the mode extracts it from the price: the tax is twenty-one, the reported base one hundred and the total with taxes one hundred twenty-one, which is exactly what supplying one hundred with no mode gives.

records.name: Rounding a value to a rounding step
records.purpose: The single rounding primitive of the tax engine. Every monetary amount the engine produces passes through it, so its tie-breaking decides every downstream figure.

operands.name: value
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency or unit being rounded
operands.source: any intermediate result of the engine: a raw base, a raw tax amount, a converted company-currency amount, a distribution share, a cash rounding target
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: rounding step
operands.source: the rounding step of the currency, or the cash rounding step of a cash rounding configuration
operands.constraints: one hundredth for a currency with two decimal places, one for a currency with no decimal place, five hundredths for a cash rounding to the nearest five cents

operands.name: method
operands.source: half away from zero everywhere in the tax engine; the other five methods are only reachable through a cash rounding configuration
operands.constraints: one of half away from zero, half toward zero, half to even, away from zero, toward zero

preconditions.condition: The rounding step is not zero and the value is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The result is zero.

procedure: When the rounding step is zero or the value is zero, return zero.
Normalise the value: when the step is smaller than one, multiply the value by the higher-accuracy reciprocal of the step; otherwise divide the value by the step.
Compute the tie-correction epsilon as two raised to the power of the binary logarithm of the absolute normalised value minus fifty.

Apply the chosen method to the normalised value, using the epsilon to decide ties: half away from zero adds the epsilon carrying the value's sign before taking the nearest integer away from zero; half toward zero subtracts it; half to even compares the fractional part against one half within the epsilon and, on a tie, moves to the even neighbour; away from zero truncates the value increased by one minus the epsilon; toward zero truncates the value increased by the epsilon.
Denormalise: when the step is smaller than one, divide by the higher-accuracy reciprocal of the step; otherwise multiply by the step.
records.formula: round_to_step( v , s , method ) : if s = 0 or v = 0 then result = 0 ; otherwise n = v × invert(s) when s < 1 , n = v ÷ s when s ≥ 1 ; e = 2 ^ ( log2( |n| ) − 50 ) ; half away from zero : r = nearest_integer_away_from_zero( n + sign(n) × e ) ; half toward zero : r = nearest_integer_away_from_zero( n − sign(n) × e ) ; half to even : i = floor(n) , f = | n − i | , r = i + ( i modulo 2 ) when | 0.5 − f | < e , otherwise r = nearest_integer_away_from_zero( n ) ; away from zero : r = truncate( n + sign(n) × ( 1 − e ) ) ; toward zero : r = truncate( n + sign(n) × e ) ; result = r ÷ invert(s) when s < 1 , r × s when s ≥ 1 . invert(s) : write s as c × 10 ^ x with fifteen significant decimal digits ; invert(s) = ( c × 10 ^ ( − x ) ) ÷ c²

rounding.what: The value handed in.
rounding.precision: The rounding step handed in; for a currency, the step recorded on that currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero by default; half toward zero, half to even, away from zero and toward zero are reachable only through a cash rounding configuration.
rounding.step: This primitive is the rounding step itself; every other calculation of the domain calls it at the moment it names.

result.name: rounded value
result.unit_or_currency: the currency or unit of the input value
result.stored_or_displayed: Returned to the calling calculation; stored only when that calculation stores it.

edge_cases.case: The value sits exactly on a half step, and its stored representation is a shade below the tie, as for two point six seven five at two decimal places.
edge_cases.outcome: The tie-correction epsilon lifts the normalised value above the tie, so the result is two point six eight rather than two point six seven.

edge_cases.case: The value is negative and exactly on a half step.
edge_cases.outcome: Half away from zero carries the half away from zero, so minus zero point zero zero five at two decimal places becomes minus zero point zero one.

edge_cases.case: The rounding step is one, for a currency with no decimal place.
edge_cases.outcome: Normalisation divides rather than multiplies and the result is a whole number of currency units.

edge_cases.case: The nearest-integer routine of the host language rounds half to even.
edge_cases.outcome: The engine's own nearest-integer-away-from-zero routine corrects it: it takes the library value, and when adding one to the input does not raise that value by exactly one, the input was on a tie and the answer is the input plus one half carrying the input's sign.

edge_cases.case: The reciprocal of the step is computed as one divided by the step.
edge_cases.outcome: A family of errors of one unit in the last binary place appears; the higher-accuracy reciprocal removes them, and for a step of one hundredth it yields exactly one hundred.

worked_examples.description: Rounding two point six seven five to two decimal places
worked_examples.narrative: The stored value is slightly below the tie, at two point six seven four nine nine nine nine, the nines continuing. Normalising by the reciprocal of one hundredth gives two hundred sixty-seven point four nine nine nine, the nines continuing. The epsilon at that magnitude is about two to the power minus forty-two, which lifts the value just above two hundred sixty-seven point five; the nearest integer away from zero is two hundred sixty-eight; denormalising gives two point six eight.

worked_examples.description: Rounding a total to the nearest five cents
worked_examples.narrative: Twelve point zero nine multiplied by the reciprocal of five hundredths is two hundred forty-one point eight; the nearest integer away from zero is two hundred forty-two; denormalising gives twelve point one zero.

records.name: Testing whether an amount is zero at a currency precision
records.purpose: Decides whether an amount is negligible, and therefore whether a redistribution pass runs, a journal item is produced or a partial reconciliation is skipped.

operands.name: value
operands.source: any amount of the engine
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: rounding step
operands.source: the rounding step of that currency
operands.constraints: strictly greater than zero

preconditions.condition: A currency, and therefore a rounding step, is known for the amount.
preconditions.otherwise: The test cannot be applied and the calculation that needed it is not meaningful.

procedure: Return true immediately when the value is exactly zero.
Otherwise round the value to the step with the method half away from zero.
Return true when the absolute value of that rounded result is strictly smaller than the step.
records.formula: is_zero( v , s ) = ( v = 0 ) or ( | round_to_step( v , s , half away from zero ) | < s )

rounding.what: The value under test, inside the test only.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero.
rounding.step: The rounding happens before the comparison; the test therefore rounds after subtracting, unlike the comparison of the next record.

result.name: zero indication
result.stored_or_displayed: Used inside the engine; never stored.

edge_cases.case: The value is six thousandths at two decimal places.
edge_cases.outcome: It rounds to one hundredth, whose absolute value is not smaller than the step, so the value is not zero.

edge_cases.case: The value is four thousandths at two decimal places.
edge_cases.outcome: It rounds to zero, so the value counts as zero.

edge_cases.case: A tax amount is zero in both currencies.
edge_cases.outcome: No journal item is produced, unless the grouping key carries the technical marker that keeps a zero line.

worked_examples.description: Four thousandths and six thousandths at two decimal places
worked_examples.narrative: Four thousandths rounds to zero point zero zero, whose absolute value is smaller than one hundredth, so the test is true. Six thousandths rounds to zero point zero one, whose absolute value equals the step and is therefore not smaller, so the test is false.

records.name: Comparing two amounts at a currency precision
records.purpose: Orders two amounts without letting a sub-unit residue decide, so that two figures a user sees as equal compare as equal.

operands.name: first amount
operands.source: any amount of the engine
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: second amount
operands.source: any amount of the engine
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: rounding step
operands.source: the rounding step of that currency
operands.constraints: strictly greater than zero

preconditions.condition: Both amounts are expressed in the same currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The comparison is meaningless; the caller must convert first.

procedure: Round each amount to the step with the method half away from zero.
Subtract the second rounded amount from the first.
Return minus one when that difference is smaller than minus half a step, plus one when it is greater than half a step, and zero otherwise.
records.formula: compare( a , b , s ) : d = round_to_step( a , s , half away from zero ) − round_to_step( b , s , half away from zero ) ; result = −1 when d < − s ÷ 2 , +1 when d > s ÷ 2 , 0 otherwise

rounding.what: Each of the two amounts, separately, before the subtraction.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero.
rounding.step: Before subtracting. The zero test of the previous record rounds after subtracting, which is why the two disagree on values such as six thousandths against two thousandths at two decimal places.

result.name: comparison indication
result.stored_or_displayed: Used inside the engine; never stored.

edge_cases.case: Six thousandths compared with two thousandths at two decimal places.
edge_cases.outcome: The first rounds to one hundredth and the second to zero, so the difference is one hundredth, which exceeds half a step: the comparison returns plus one. The zero test on their difference of four thousandths would have said the two are equal.

edge_cases.case: The two amounts are equal.
edge_cases.outcome: The difference is zero, which is neither below minus half a step nor above half a step, so the comparison returns zero.

worked_examples.description: Six thousandths against two thousandths at two decimal places
worked_examples.narrative: Rounding first gives one hundredth and zero; their difference of one hundredth is greater than half a step of five thousandths, so the first amount is the greater one.

records.name: Rounding to the line currency and to the company currency
records.purpose: Names the two rounding steps every amount of a base line is reduced to: the currency the price is expressed in, and the currency the ledger is kept in.

operands.name: value
operands.source: any amount of the engine
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: line currency rounding step
operands.source: the rounding step recorded on the base line's currency
operands.constraints: strictly positive

operands.name: company currency rounding step
operands.source: the rounding step recorded on the company's currency
operands.constraints: strictly positive

preconditions.condition: The base line resolved a currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The engine has no rounding step and cannot round the line's amounts.

procedure: To round to the line currency, call the rounding primitive with the line currency's rounding step and the method half away from zero.
To round to the company currency, call it with the company currency's rounding step and the same method.
records.formula: round_to_line_currency( v ) = round_to_step( v , line currency step , half away from zero ) ; round_to_company_currency( v ) = round_to_step( v , company currency step , half away from zero )

rounding.what: Any amount the engine writes or compares.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the named currency, together with the number of decimal places derived from it.
rounding.method: Half away from zero.
rounding.step: Immediately after the single-line computation under the round-per-line method, and in the document-wide passes under the round-per-tax method.

result.name: rounded amount
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the tax details block and, through it, on the journal items.

edge_cases.case: The line currency and the company currency are the same.
edge_cases.outcome: Both roundings use the same step; the two amounts of a pair stay equal.

edge_cases.case: The company currency has no decimal place while the line currency has two.
edge_cases.outcome: Each currency is rounded and redistributed independently, so an allocation may land on one line in one currency and on another line in the other.

worked_examples.description: One amount rounded to two currencies of different precision
worked_examples.narrative: Seventeen point two two four rounds to seventeen point two two at a step of one hundredth, and to seventeen at a step of one.

records.name: Flattening and ordering a set of taxes
records.purpose: Turns the taxes attached to a line into the ordered list the engine evaluates, resolving every Group of Taxes into its children while remembering the group.

operands.name: input taxes
operands.source: the taxes recorded on the base line
operands.constraints: may contain Groups of Taxes; nested groups are forbidden

operands.name: sequence of each tax
operands.source: the sequence field of the tax
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: identifier of each tax
operands.source: the tax's own identifier
operands.constraints: absent on a tax that has not been stored yet

preconditions.condition: No Group of Taxes contains another Group of Taxes.
preconditions.otherwise: The configuration is refused when the group is saved, with the message "Nested group of taxes are not allowed."; one flattening pass therefore suffices.

procedure: Sort the input taxes by sequence ascending, then by identifier ascending; a tax that has not been stored yet sorts as if its identifier were absent, which places it first among taxes of equal sequence.
Walk the sorted input in order.
For a Group of Taxes, sort its children by the same key and append them in that order, recording the group against each child.
For any other tax, append the tax itself.
Never append the same tax twice.
records.formula: flattened = concatenation , over the input taxes sorted by ( sequence ascending , identifier ascending ) , of ( the children of the tax sorted by the same key , when the tax is a Group of Taxes ) or ( the tax itself , otherwise ) , duplicates removed

rounding.what: Nothing.
rounding.method: Not applicable.
rounding.step: This step produces an ordering, not an amount.

result.name: flattened tax list and the map from each tax to its originating group
result.stored_or_displayed: Held in the engine; the originating group is carried onto every produced tax entry and onto the journal item it becomes.

edge_cases.case: A group's own sequence differs from its children's sequences.
edge_cases.outcome: The group is evaluated at the position of the group's own sequence and its children keep their relative order inside that position: the input naming a group of sequence high containing three taxes, plus two ungrouped taxes, evaluates the three children together at the group's position.

edge_cases.case: The same tax appears twice, once directly and once through a group.
edge_cases.outcome: It is appended only once, at its first occurrence.

edge_cases.case: A tax has not been stored yet.
edge_cases.outcome: It sorts before saved taxes of the same sequence; an implementation that sorts it last will preview a document differently from the saved result.

worked_examples.description: A group evaluated at its own position, its children keeping their order

inputs.input_taxes: the tax named G, then the group named B containing the taxes named A, D and F, then the tax named E, then the tax named C, with the letters ordered alphabetically by sequence

worked_examples.narrative: The group named B sorts at its own position, before the taxes named C and E and after nothing; its three children are emitted in their own order, so the evaluation order is A, D, F, then C, then E, then G.

records.name: Filtering the flattened tax list
records.purpose: Removes taxes from an evaluation without unlinking them from their parent group, which is how withholding taxes are kept out of a document total and how a caller restricts a computation to a subset of taxes.

operands.name: flattened tax list
operands.source: the flattening step
operands.constraints: already ordered

operands.name: filter predicate
operands.source: the base line's optional filter, or the filter the engine installs to drop withholding taxes
operands.constraints: optional

preconditions.condition: The flattening step has already run.
preconditions.otherwise: Filtering before flattening would remove a whole group instead of a child and would lose the surviving children.

procedure: When no predicate was supplied, keep the whole flattened list.
Otherwise keep only the taxes that satisfy the predicate, in their existing order.
Leave the recorded originating group of every surviving tax untouched.
records.formula: filtered = the taxes t of the flattened list for which predicate( t ) is true ; originating group of t is unchanged

rounding.what: Nothing.
rounding.method: Not applicable.
rounding.step: This step selects taxes, not amounts.

result.name: filtered tax list
result.stored_or_displayed: Held in the engine for the batching step.

edge_cases.case: Every child of a group is removed by the filter.
edge_cases.outcome: The group contributes nothing and no journal item names it.

edge_cases.case: Some children of a group survive.
edge_cases.outcome: Their entries still carry the group, because filtering happens after flattening.

edge_cases.case: No caller asked for withholding taxes.
edge_cases.outcome: The engine installs a predicate that removes every withholding tax, so a withholding tax never appears in a document total.

worked_examples.description: A group of two children, one of them filtered out
worked_examples.narrative: One child is dropped; the survivor still records the group, so the journal item it produces names the group as its originator.

records.name: Grouping consecutive taxes into batches
records.purpose: Decides which taxes must be solved together, because extracting several price-included percentage taxes from one price is a single division rather than a chain of divisions.

operands.name: filtered tax list
operands.source: the flattening and filtering steps
operands.constraints: in evaluation order

operands.name: computation kind of each tax
operands.source: the tax's computation kind: fixed amount, percentage, division or custom formula
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: price-inclusion flag of each tax
operands.source: the tax's own price-inclusion flag
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: affects base of subsequent taxes flag of each tax
operands.source: the tax
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: base affected by previous taxes flag of each tax
operands.source: the tax
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: special mode
operands.source: the base line
operands.constraints: absent, total excluded or total included

preconditions.condition: The list is the flattened and filtered list, in evaluation order.
preconditions.otherwise: Batching a list that still contains groups would produce batches that do not match the evaluation.

procedure: Start with an empty batch and with the flag saying the previously examined tax accepts being affected set to false.
Walk the filtered list backwards, that is from the last tax in evaluation order to the first.

When the batch is not empty, the tax joins it only when all four of these hold: it has the same computation kind as the batch's first member; either a special mode is active or it has the same price-inclusion flag as the batch's first member; it has the same affects-base flag as the batch's first member; and either it does not affect the base of subsequent taxes, or it does affect it and the previously examined tax does not accept being affected.
When any of the four fails, close the current batch, assign that batch to each of its members, and start a new one.
Set the flag saying the previously examined tax accepts being affected to this tax's own base-affected-by-previous-taxes flag, then append this tax to the batch.
Close the last batch when the walk ends.
records.formula: a batch is a maximal run of consecutive taxes, taken in reverse evaluation order, such that same_kind = true and ( special mode active or same_inclusion = true ) and same_affects_base = true and ( affects_base = false or previous_accepts_being_affected = false ) ; the flag previous_accepts_being_affected is set to the examined tax's own base-affected-by-previous-taxes flag after the test and before the next iteration

rounding.what: Nothing.
rounding.method: Not applicable.
rounding.step: Batching produces a partition, not an amount; it decides which division the price-included extraction performs.

result.name: the batch of each tax
result.stored_or_displayed: Held in the engine; the batch total is subtracted from the reported base of a price-included tax and the batch percentage drives the extraction factor.

edge_cases.case: Two price-included percentage taxes of ten percent each, neither affecting the other's base.
edge_cases.outcome: They form one batch, so the extraction divides by one plus zero point two rather than dividing twice by one plus zero point one.

edge_cases.case: The first tax affects the base of subsequent taxes and the second accepts being affected.
edge_cases.outcome: The fourth condition fails and the two taxes form two batches of one, evaluated in cascade.

edge_cases.case: A special mode is active.
edge_cases.outcome: The price-inclusion condition is waived, because the mode overrides every tax's own flag.

edge_cases.case: Because the walk is backwards, the previously examined tax is the tax that comes after in evaluation order.
edge_cases.outcome: The fourth condition therefore tests the acceptance of the following tax, not of the preceding one.

worked_examples.description: Two price-included percentage taxes of ten percent each in one batch

inputs.taxes: a ten percent price-included tax of sequence one and a ten percent price-included tax of sequence two, neither affecting the base of the other

worked_examples.narrative: Walking backwards, the second tax opens a batch and the first joins it because all four conditions hold. The batch percentage is zero point two, the extraction factor is one divided by one point two, each tax amount is eight point three three three three recurring, and the base is one hundred less the two amounts.

worked_examples.description: The same two taxes, but the first affects the base and the second accepts it

inputs.taxes: a ten percent tax of sequence one that affects the base of subsequent taxes and a ten percent tax of sequence two whose base is affected by previous taxes

worked_examples.narrative: Walking backwards, the second tax opens a batch and sets the flag saying the previously examined tax accepts being affected. The first tax affects the base while that flag is true, so the fourth condition fails and it cannot join: two batches of one each, evaluated in cascade.

records.name: The percentage of a batch
records.purpose: The single quantity from which the price-included extraction factor and the division multiplier are built; it is the sum of the rates of every tax solved together.

operands.name: rate of each tax in the batch
operands.source: the amount field of each tax of the batch
operands.constraints: may be negative, as on a reverse-charge or withholding tax

preconditions.condition: The batch has been closed by the batching step.
preconditions.otherwise: A partial batch would give a factor that does not match the taxes actually extracted together.

procedure: Sum the rate of every tax that belongs to the batch.
Divide that sum by one hundred.
records.formula: batch_percentage( B ) = ( sum over t in B of t.amount ) ÷ 100

rounding.what: Nothing.
rounding.method: Not applicable.
rounding.step: The batch percentage is never rounded; rounding it would move every extracted amount.

result.name: batch percentage
result.stored_or_displayed: Held in the engine and consumed by the price-included and the division formulas.

edge_cases.case: The batch percentage is exactly minus one.
edge_cases.outcome: The price-included extraction factor is set to zero instead of dividing by zero, so every tax of the batch has an amount of zero.

edge_cases.case: The batch percentage is exactly one.
edge_cases.outcome: The division multiplier is set to one instead of dividing by zero, so the tax equals the base.

edge_cases.case: The batch has one member.
edge_cases.outcome: The batch percentage is that tax's own rate divided by one hundred.

worked_examples.description: A batch of two percentage taxes of ten percent
worked_examples.narrative: Ten plus ten is twenty; divided by one hundred that is zero point two.

records.name: The amount of a fixed-amount tax
records.purpose: Computes a per-unit charge such as an environmental levy, which does not depend on the base and is evaluated first so that it can move the price a price-included batch is extracted from.

operands.name: quantity
operands.source: the base line
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative

operands.name: unit price after discount
operands.source: the base line, discount already applied
operands.constraints: only its sign is used

operands.name: tax rate
operands.source: the amount field of the tax
operands.constraints: none

preconditions.condition: The tax's computation kind is fixed amount.
preconditions.otherwise: Another formula of section four applies.

preconditions.condition: The evaluation is in the first pass, before the price-included and the price-excluded passes.
preconditions.otherwise: A price-included batch would be extracted from a price that does not yet include the fixed charge.

procedure: Take the sign of the unit price after the discount: minus one when that price is strictly negative, plus one otherwise.
Multiply that sign by the quantity and by the tax's per-unit amount.
Ignore the raw base entirely.
records.formula: tax_amount = sign_of_price × quantity × tax.amount , where sign_of_price = −1 when the unit price after the discount is strictly negative and +1 otherwise

rounding.what: The tax amount.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the line currency, and of the company currency for the converted amount.
rounding.method: Half away from zero.
rounding.step: Immediately after the amount is produced under the round-per-line method; in the document-wide passes under the round-per-tax method.

result.name: tax amount of the fixed tax
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the tax details block and posted as a tax journal item.

edge_cases.case: The unit price after discount is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The fixed amount is negated, so the tax follows the sign of the line.

edge_cases.case: The quantity is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The tax amount is zero, because the formula multiplies by the quantity.

edge_cases.case: The fixed tax is flagged as affecting the base of subsequent taxes and a later tax accepts being affected.
edge_cases.outcome: The later tax's base grows by the fixed amount.

edge_cases.case: The fixed tax is discounted proportionally by a global discount.
edge_cases.outcome: It is excluded: a fixed tax is a per-unit charge and cannot be scaled by a discount percentage.

worked_examples.description: Mandatory example three: seven units at fifteen with a levy of five hundredths per unit and a twenty percent tax
worked_examples.narrative: The raw base is seven times fifteen, that is one hundred five. The levy is plus one times seven times five hundredths, that is zero point three five. The twenty percent tax is computed on the same base of one hundred five, because the levy does not affect the base of subsequent taxes, giving twenty-one. The tax total is twenty-one point three five and the grand total one hundred twenty-six point three five.

worked_examples.description: The same line with the levy affecting the base of the twenty percent tax
worked_examples.narrative: The second tax's base becomes one hundred five point three five, its amount twenty-one point zero seven, the tax total twenty-one point four two and the grand total one hundred twenty-six point four two.

records.name: The amount of a percentage tax that is price-excluded
records.purpose: The ordinary case: a rate applied on top of a base, giving the tax a customer pays in addition to the price.

operands.name: raw base
operands.source: the line's raw base plus any extra base propagated to this tax
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative

operands.name: tax rate
operands.source: the amount field of the tax
operands.constraints: may be negative for a reverse charge or a withholding tax

preconditions.condition: The tax's effective price-inclusion flag is false and its computation kind is percentage.
preconditions.otherwise: The price-included formula or a formula of another kind applies.

preconditions.condition: The evaluation is in the third pass, walking the list forwards.
preconditions.otherwise: A tax that swells the base of a later tax would be applied out of order.

procedure: Take the raw base handed to this tax, which already includes any extra base propagated to it.
Multiply it by the tax rate and divide by one hundred.
records.formula: tax_amount = raw_base × tax.amount ÷ 100

rounding.what: The tax amount and, separately, the reported base.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the line currency and of the company currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero.
rounding.step: Immediately after the amount is produced under the round-per-line method; in the document-wide passes under the round-per-tax method.

result.name: tax amount
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the tax details block, shown in the totals block and posted as a tax journal item.

edge_cases.case: The raw base is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The tax amount is zero.

edge_cases.case: The rate is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The amount is negative; a distribution line with a negative factor turns it into the reverse-charge half, and the withholding flow negates it again to obtain a positive amount withheld.

edge_cases.case: The line is under the special mode saying the price is the total with taxes.
edge_cases.outcome: The effective price-inclusion flag becomes true and the price-included formula applies instead.

worked_examples.description: Mandatory example one: one unit at one hundred with a twenty-one percent price-excluded tax
worked_examples.narrative: One hundred times twenty-one divided by one hundred is twenty-one; the base stays one hundred and the grand total is one hundred twenty-one.

records.name: The amount of a percentage tax that is price-included
records.purpose: Extracts a rate from a price that already contains it, so that the untaxed amount and the tax add back exactly to the price the customer sees.

operands.name: raw base
operands.source: the line's raw base plus any extra base propagated to this tax
operands.constraints: the price with the batch's taxes still inside it

operands.name: batch percentage
operands.source: the sum of the rates of every tax of the batch divided by one hundred
operands.constraints: the guard applies when it equals minus one

operands.name: tax rate
operands.source: the amount field of the tax
operands.constraints: none

preconditions.condition: The tax's effective price-inclusion flag is true and its computation kind is percentage.
preconditions.otherwise: The price-excluded formula or a formula of another kind applies.

preconditions.condition: The batch percentage is not exactly minus one.
preconditions.otherwise: The extraction factor is set to zero and every tax of the batch has an amount of zero, instead of a division by zero.

preconditions.condition: The evaluation is in the second pass, walking the list backwards.
preconditions.otherwise: The extraction would be applied to a price from which a later tax has not yet been removed.

procedure: Sum the rates of every tax in the batch and divide by one hundred to obtain the batch percentage.
Compute the extraction factor as one divided by one plus the batch percentage, or zero when the batch percentage is exactly minus one.
Multiply the raw base by the extraction factor, then by the tax rate, then divide by one hundred.
The reported base of the tax is the raw base less the total of the batch's amounts, computed in the base pass.
records.formula: total_percentage = batch_percentage( batch ) ; to_price_excluded = 1 ÷ ( 1 + total_percentage ) , or 0 when total_percentage = −1 ; tax_amount = raw_base × to_price_excluded × tax.amount ÷ 100

rounding.what: The tax amount and the reported base.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the line currency and of the company currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero.
rounding.step: Immediately under the round-per-line method; in the document-wide passes under the round-per-tax method. The extraction factor itself is never rounded.

result.name: tax amount
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the tax details block; the base reported for the tax is the price less the batch total.

edge_cases.case: The batch percentage is exactly minus one hundred percent.
edge_cases.outcome: The extraction factor is zero and every tax of the batch has an amount of zero.

edge_cases.case: Two price-included taxes share a batch.
edge_cases.outcome: One single division by one plus the summed percentage is performed, not two successive divisions, which would give a different base.

edge_cases.case: The extraction leaves a residue that cannot be represented in the currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The rounded tax and the rounded base still add back to the price, because the base is derived by subtracting the batch total from the price.

worked_examples.description: Mandatory example two: one unit at one hundred twenty-one with a twenty-one percent price-included tax
worked_examples.narrative: One divided by one point two one is zero point eight two six four four six two eight zero nine nine one seven three five; one hundred twenty-one multiplied by that factor and by zero point two one is twenty-one, and the base is one hundred twenty-one less twenty-one, that is one hundred.

worked_examples.description: A price that leaves a residue, under the round-per-tax method
worked_examples.narrative: Twenty-one point five three divided by one point two one multiplied by zero point two one is three point seven three six six one one five seven zero two four seven nine three four; the raw base is the remainder; rounding gives three point seven four and seventeen point seven nine, which add back to twenty-one point five three.

worked_examples.description: Two price-included taxes of ten percent in one batch
worked_examples.narrative: The single division by one point two gives each tax eight point three three three three recurring and leaves a base of eighty-three point three three three three, unlike two successive divisions by one point one.

records.name: The amount of a division tax that is price-excluded
records.purpose: Computes a tax expressed as a percentage of the total including the tax, applied on top of a price that does not yet contain it.

operands.name: raw base
operands.source: the line's raw base plus any extra base propagated to this tax
operands.constraints: the amount without the tax

operands.name: batch percentage
operands.source: the sum of the rates of every tax of the batch divided by one hundred
operands.constraints: the guard applies when it equals one

operands.name: tax rate
operands.source: the amount field of the tax
operands.constraints: none

preconditions.condition: The tax's computation kind is division and its effective price-inclusion flag is false.
preconditions.otherwise: The price-included division formula or a formula of another kind applies.

preconditions.condition: The batch percentage is not exactly one.
preconditions.otherwise: The multiplier is set to one, so the tax equals the base, instead of a division by zero.

preconditions.condition: The evaluation is in the third pass.
preconditions.otherwise: The base would not yet carry the amounts of the taxes that swell it.

procedure: Sum the rates of every tax in the batch and divide by one hundred.
Set the included-base multiplier to one when that sum equals one, and to one less that sum otherwise.
Multiply the raw base by the tax rate, divide by one hundred, then divide by the included-base multiplier.
records.formula: total_percentage = batch_percentage( batch ) ; included_base_multiplier = 1 when total_percentage = 1 , = 1 − total_percentage otherwise ; tax_amount = raw_base × tax.amount ÷ 100 ÷ included_base_multiplier

rounding.what: The tax amount.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the line currency and of the company currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero.
rounding.step: Immediately under the round-per-line method; in the document-wide passes under the round-per-tax method.

result.name: tax amount
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the tax details block; the base reported is the raw base, because the tax is added on top.

edge_cases.case: The batch percentage is exactly one hundred percent.
edge_cases.outcome: The multiplier is one, so the tax equals the base and no division by zero occurs.

edge_cases.case: The raw base is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The tax amount is zero.

edge_cases.case: Only division taxes that are all price-included contribute to a tax group.
edge_cases.outcome: The totals block shows the tax-inclusive amount as that group's displayed base.

worked_examples.description: Mandatory example four: one unit at one hundred eighty with a ten percent division tax, price-excluded
worked_examples.narrative: One hundred eighty multiplied by zero point one and divided by zero point nine is twenty, which is indeed ten percent of the grand total of two hundred.

records.name: The amount of a division tax that is price-included
records.purpose: Computes a tax expressed as a percentage of the total including the tax when the price handed in is already that total; it is the exact inverse of the price-excluded division tax.

operands.name: raw base
operands.source: the line's raw base plus any extra base propagated to this tax
operands.constraints: the amount with the tax inside it

operands.name: tax rate
operands.source: the amount field of the tax
operands.constraints: none

preconditions.condition: The tax's computation kind is division and its effective price-inclusion flag is true.
preconditions.otherwise: The price-excluded division formula applies.

preconditions.condition: The evaluation is in the second pass, walking backwards.
preconditions.otherwise: The extraction would run on a price from which a later tax has not been removed.

procedure: Multiply the raw base by the tax rate and divide by one hundred; no batch multiplier is involved, because the price already contains the tax.
The reported base is the price less the batch total, computed in the base pass.
records.formula: tax_amount = raw_base × tax.amount ÷ 100

rounding.what: The tax amount and the reported base.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the line currency and of the company currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero.
rounding.step: Immediately under the round-per-line method; in the document-wide passes under the round-per-tax method.

result.name: tax amount
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the tax details block and posted as a tax journal item.

edge_cases.case: The same transaction is expressed with the price-excluded form.
edge_cases.outcome: One hundred eighty excluded and two hundred included describe the same transaction and produce the same untaxed total, tax and grand total.

edge_cases.case: The raw base is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The tax amount is zero.

worked_examples.description: One unit at two hundred with a ten percent division tax, price-included
worked_examples.narrative: Two hundred multiplied by zero point one is twenty; the base is two hundred less twenty, that is one hundred eighty.

records.name: The amount of a custom-formula tax
records.purpose: Lets a jurisdiction express a charge that none of the four standard kinds can, as a single arithmetic expression over the price, the quantity, the base, the product and the unit of measure.

operands.name: unit price after discount
operands.source: the base line
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: quantity
operands.source: the base line
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: base
operands.source: the raw base handed to this tax, including any propagated extra base
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: product field values
operands.source: a flat table of the product's non-relational field values
operands.constraints: no relation may be read

operands.name: unit of measure field values
operands.source: a flat table of the unit of measure's non-relational field values
operands.constraints: no relation may be read

preconditions.condition: The Custom Formula Taxes capability is installed.
preconditions.otherwise: The computation kind is not offered and no such tax can exist.

preconditions.condition: The expression parses as one arithmetic expression.
preconditions.otherwise: The tax is refused with "Invalid formula".

preconditions.condition: Every field read exists on the product or the unit of measure and is not a relation.
preconditions.otherwise: The tax is refused with "Field '<the field name>' is not accessible".

preconditions.condition: Every construct used is one of the permitted ones: the expression, a name, a call, an index read, a constant, addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, the boolean operators and and or, the four comparisons less-than, less-than-or-equal, greater-than and greater-than-or-equal, and unary plus and minus.
preconditions.otherwise: The tax is refused with "Invalid AST node: <the construct name>".

preconditions.condition: Every constant is a whole number, a decimal or the empty value.
preconditions.otherwise: The tax is refused with "Only int, float or None are allowed as constant values".

preconditions.condition: Every name is one of the five permitted names and is only read.
preconditions.otherwise: The tax is refused with "Unknown identifier: <the name>" or "Only read access to identifiers is allowed".

preconditions.condition: Every call is to the function that returns the smaller of its arguments or the function that returns the larger, with positional arguments only.
preconditions.otherwise: The tax is refused with "Unknown function call" or "Kwargs are not allowed".

preconditions.condition: Every index read is on the product table or the unit of measure table with a text constant index.
preconditions.otherwise: The tax is refused with "Only product['string'] or uom['string'] read-access is allowed".

preconditions.condition: Every value of the evaluation context survives a round trip through a neutral text encoding.
preconditions.otherwise: The evaluation raises "Only primitive types are allowed in python tax formula context.", reproduced verbatim.

procedure: Rewrite every attribute read on the product or the unit of measure as an index read and record the field name, before validating.
Validate the expression against the grammar, at save time and again at every evaluation.
Build the evaluation context with exactly the five permitted names.
Evaluate the expression in the first pass, alongside fixed-amount taxes, so that the result can influence a price-included batch.
Yield zero rather than an error when the expression divides by zero.
records.formula: tax_amount = the value of the tax's expression evaluated over the context ( price_unit , quantity , base , product , uom ) ; a division by zero during the evaluation yields 0 ; the default expression of a new custom-formula tax is tax_amount = price_unit × 0.1

rounding.what: The value the expression returns.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the line currency and of the company currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero.
rounding.step: Immediately after the expression is evaluated under the round-per-line method; in the document-wide passes under the round-per-tax method. Nothing is rounded inside the expression.

result.name: tax amount
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the tax details block and posted as a tax journal item.

edge_cases.case: The expression divides by zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The result is zero rather than an error.

edge_cases.case: The tax is placed in a price-included batch.
edge_cases.outcome: It behaves exactly like a fixed tax: it is computed first and its result is never divided out of the batch.

edge_cases.case: A global discount or a down payment scales the document.
edge_cases.outcome: A custom-formula tax is not discountable and is excluded from every proportional operation, like a fixed tax.

worked_examples.description: The default expression on a line of one unit at one hundred

inputs.expression: the unit price multiplied by one tenth

worked_examples.narrative: The default expression of a new custom-formula tax multiplies the unit price by one tenth, so a price of one hundred gives a tax of ten, whatever the base is.

records.name: The contribution of a Group of Taxes
records.purpose: States that a group is a container and never an amount, and fixes what the children produce and what the produced entries record.

operands.name: children of the group
operands.source: the group's children
operands.constraints: no child may itself be a group

operands.name: raw base
operands.source: the base line
operands.constraints: none

preconditions.condition: The group has at least one child that survives the filter.
preconditions.otherwise: The group contributes nothing and no journal item names it.

preconditions.condition: No child is itself a Group of Taxes.
preconditions.otherwise: The configuration is refused with "Nested group of taxes are not allowed."

procedure: Replace the group by its children during flattening, in the children's own order, at the position of the group's own sequence.
Compute each child by the formula of its own computation kind.
Record the group on each child's result so that the produced accounting entry names it as its originator group.
Never compute an amount for the group itself.
records.formula: group_amount = 0 ; the amounts are those of the children , each computed by the formula of its own computation kind , and each result records the group as its originator group

rounding.what: Nothing at the group level; each child's amount is rounded by its own rule.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the line currency and of the company currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero.
rounding.step: As for each child's own computation kind.

result.name: one tax result per child
result.stored_or_displayed: One tax journal item per child; the totals block shows each child under its own tax group, which may or may not be the same one.

edge_cases.case: A filter removes every child.
edge_cases.outcome: The group contributes nothing and no journal item names it.

edge_cases.case: The children belong to different tax groups.
edge_cases.outcome: The totals block shows them on separate lines, under their own tax groups.

edge_cases.case: The group's children have different sequences.
edge_cases.outcome: They keep their relative order inside the position fixed by the group's own sequence.

worked_examples.description: Mandatory example five: a group of a ten percent and a five percent tax on one unit at one hundred
worked_examples.narrative: Both children work on the same base of one hundred, giving ten and five. Two tax accounting entries are produced, one per child, each naming the group as its originator group.

records.name: Propagating one tax's amount into another tax's base
records.purpose: Decides, once a tax's amount is known, which other taxes see that amount added to or removed from their base, so that a cascade of taxes and a price-included extraction agree on what each tax is charged on.

operands.name: amount of the tax just computed
operands.source: the formula of that tax's computation kind
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: own price-inclusion flag of that tax
operands.source: the tax's configured flag, not the effective flag forced by a special mode
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: special mode of the base line
operands.source: the base line
operands.constraints: absent, total excluded or total included

operands.name: affects base of subsequent taxes flag
operands.source: the tax
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: base affected by previous taxes flag of every other tax
operands.source: each other tax
operands.constraints: none

preconditions.condition: The amount of the tax is known.
preconditions.otherwise: Nothing is propagated; propagation always follows a computed amount.

preconditions.condition: The receiving tax's amount is not yet computed, for the accumulator that feeds the amount.
preconditions.otherwise: Only the accumulator that feeds the reported base is updated, because a computed amount must never change afterwards.

procedure: Maintain two accumulators per tax: the extra base that feeds the computation of that tax's amount, updated only while that amount is still unknown, and the extra base that feeds the base reported for that tax, always updated.
Let the taxes before the current tax's batch in evaluation order be the earlier taxes, and those after it the later taxes.

When the tax is price-included and the mode is absent or total included and it affects the base: subtract its amount from every later tax that does not accept being affected, and from every earlier tax.
When the tax is price-included and the mode is absent or total included and it does not affect the base: subtract its amount from every later tax and from every earlier tax.
When the tax is price-included and the mode is total excluded and it affects the base: add its amount to every later tax that does accept being affected.
When the tax is price-included and the mode is total excluded and it does not affect the base: do nothing.
When the tax is price-excluded and the mode is absent or total excluded and it affects the base: add its amount to every later tax that does accept being affected.
When the tax is price-excluded and the mode is absent or total excluded and it does not affect the base: do nothing.
When the tax is price-excluded and the mode is total included and it affects the base: subtract its amount from every earlier tax.
When the tax is price-excluded and the mode is total included and it does not affect the base: subtract its amount from every later tax and from every earlier tax.
records.formula: for the tax T of amount A : included and mode absent or total included and affects base : extra_base( t ) = extra_base( t ) − A for every later t that does not accept being affected and for every earlier t ; included and mode absent or total included and does not affect base : extra_base( t ) = extra_base( t ) − A for every later t and every earlier t ; included and mode total excluded and affects base : extra_base( t ) = extra_base( t ) + A for every later t that accepts being affected ; included and mode total excluded and does not affect base : no change ; excluded and mode absent or total excluded and affects base : extra_base( t ) = extra_base( t ) + A for every later t that accepts being affected ; excluded and mode absent or total excluded and does not affect base : no change ; excluded and mode total included and affects base : extra_base( t ) = extra_base( t ) − A for every earlier t ; excluded and mode total included and does not affect base : extra_base( t ) = extra_base( t ) − A for every later t and every earlier t

rounding.what: Nothing at this step; the amount propagated is the amount as it stands.
rounding.precision: Under the round-per-line method the amount was already rounded to the line currency before propagation; under the round-per-tax method it is the raw amount.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, when the amount was rounded.
rounding.step: Propagation runs immediately after an amount is produced and after the mirror onto a reverse-charge half, and before the next tax of the pass is evaluated.

result.name: the two extra-base accumulators of every tax
result.stored_or_displayed: Consumed by the amount formulas and by the base pass; never stored.

edge_cases.case: A tax's amount has already been computed when another tax tries to feed its computation accumulator.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the accumulator feeding the reported base is updated, so a computed amount never changes.

edge_cases.case: A price-included tax carries a special mode.
edge_cases.outcome: The row of the table is chosen by the tax's own configured price-inclusion flag, not by the effective flag the mode forces.

edge_cases.case: The mode is total excluded and a price-included tax affects the base.
edge_cases.outcome: The caller already handed a price with the included taxes removed, so the amount must be added back to reconstruct the base of the taxes it is meant to swell.

edge_cases.case: The mode is total included and a price-excluded tax affects the base.
edge_cases.outcome: The later taxes already contain it by construction, so only the earlier taxes have it removed.

worked_examples.description: Mandatory example six: a ten percent tax affecting the base of a five percent tax, both price-excluded, one unit at one hundred

inputs.tax_A: ten percent, sequence one, price-excluded, affects the base of subsequent taxes
inputs.tax_B: five percent, sequence two, price-excluded, base affected by previous taxes

worked_examples.narrative: Batching gives two batches of one, because the first tax affects the base while the flag saying the following tax accepts being affected is true. In the price-excluded pass the first tax has base one hundred and amount ten, and adds ten to both accumulators of the second tax; the second has base one hundred ten and amount five point five zero. The base pass gives the second tax a base of one hundred ten and the first a base of one hundred, and records the second tax as the first tax's downstream tax. The untaxed total is the base of the first entry, one hundred.

worked_examples.description: The same chain with the first tax price-included at a price of one hundred ten

inputs.tax_A: ten percent, sequence one, price-included, affects the base of subsequent taxes
inputs.tax_B: five percent, sequence two, price-excluded, base affected by previous taxes

worked_examples.narrative: The price-included pass extracts ten from one hundred ten; propagation changes nothing because there is no later tax that refuses to be affected and no earlier tax. The second tax works on one hundred ten and gives five point five zero. In the base pass the first tax's base is one hundred ten less its own batch total of ten, that is one hundred. The totals are identical to the price-excluded variant.

records.name: Computing one base line
records.purpose: The end-to-end single-line algorithm: it turns a price, a quantity and a set of taxes into the tax details block that every later step of the engine consumes.

operands.name: taxes
operands.source: the base line
operands.constraints: may contain Groups of Taxes

operands.name: unit price after discount
operands.source: the base line
operands.constraints: the discount is applied before the engine is called

operands.name: quantity
operands.source: the base line
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative

operands.name: currency rounding step
operands.source: the line's currency
operands.constraints: strictly positive

operands.name: document-wide rounding method
operands.source: the company
operands.constraints: round per line or round per tax

operands.name: product and unit of measure
operands.source: the base line
operands.constraints: used by custom-formula taxes and to collect product tags

operands.name: special mode
operands.source: the base line
operands.constraints: absent, total excluded or total included

operands.name: filter predicate
operands.source: the base line
operands.constraints: optional

preconditions.condition: The base line has been prepared, so that every key has a resolved value or its fallback.
preconditions.otherwise: The engine has no price, no quantity and no currency and cannot compute.

preconditions.condition: A currency is resolved for the line.
preconditions.otherwise: No rounding step exists and the amounts cannot be rounded.

procedure: Flatten, filter and batch the taxes.

Initialise one record per tax with the tax, its effective price-inclusion flag, two zeroed extra-base accumulators, the parent group and the batch; the effective flag is false when the tax has a negative distribution factor, otherwise true under the mode total included and false under the mode total excluded, otherwise the tax's own flag.
Create a second, mirror record marked as the reverse-charge half for every tax with a negative distribution factor.
Compute the raw base as the quantity multiplied by the unit price, and round it to the currency step immediately under the round-per-line method.
First pass, walking backwards: evaluate every fixed-amount and custom-formula tax whose amount is not yet known.
Second pass, walking backwards: evaluate every tax whose effective price-inclusion flag is true and whose amount is not yet known.
Third pass, walking forwards: evaluate every tax whose effective price-inclusion flag is false and whose amount is not yet known.
Whenever an amount is produced, round it to the currency step immediately under the round-per-line method, mirror it negated onto the reverse-charge half when there is one, then run the propagation.

Base pass, walking backwards with a stack of subsequent taxes that starts empty: for each tax whose amount is known, compute the batch total, add the extra base for the reported base to the raw base, subtract the batch total when the effective price-inclusion flag is true and the mode is absent or total included, record the base, set the downstream tax list to the current stack when the tax affects the base of subsequent taxes and to the empty list otherwise, copy both onto the reverse-charge half, and push the tax on the stack when it accepts being affected by previous taxes.
Assemble the result list in the order the records were created, that is the flattened order, inserting each reverse-charge half immediately after its positive half.

Set the untaxed total to the base of the first entry of the result list and the total with taxes to that untaxed total plus the sum of every entry's tax amount; when the result list is empty, set both totals to the raw base.
records.formula: raw_base = quantity × unit_price_after_discount ( rounded to the currency step immediately under round per line ) ; batch_total = sum of the amounts of every tax of this tax's batch + sum of the reverse-charge halves of those of them that have one ; base = raw_base + extra_base_for_base ; base = base − batch_total when the effective price-inclusion flag is true and the special mode is absent or total included ; total_excluded = base of the first entry of the result list ; total_included = total_excluded + sum of every entry's tax amount

rounding.what: The raw base and every tax amount.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the line currency, and of the company currency for the converted amounts.
rounding.method: Half away from zero.
rounding.step: Under the round-per-line method the raw base is rounded before the passes and each amount immediately after it is produced; under the round-per-tax method nothing is rounded here and everything is rounded by the document-wide passes.

result.name: the tax details block of the base line
result.unit_or_currency: the line currency and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Held on the base line; consumed by the document-wide rounding, the totals block and the accounting derivation.

edge_cases.case: The line carries no tax at all.
edge_cases.outcome: The untaxed total and the total with taxes both equal the raw base, and the totals block still counts the line in the untaxed amount.

edge_cases.case: The quantity is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The raw base is zero; percentage and division taxes give zero and a fixed tax also gives zero, because it multiplies by the quantity.

edge_cases.case: A tax has a negative distribution factor.
edge_cases.outcome: Its effective price-inclusion flag is forced to false, whatever its own flag says, and a mirror record carrying the negated amount is created for the reverse-charge half.

edge_cases.case: The untaxed total is taken as the raw base rather than as the base of the first entry.
edge_cases.outcome: Price-included taxes break, because the first entry's base is the one from which the included taxes have already been removed.

worked_examples.description: One unit at one hundred twenty-one with a twenty-one percent price-included tax, carried through the passes
worked_examples.narrative: The first pass finds nothing, the second pass extracts twenty-one, the third pass finds nothing. The base pass subtracts the batch total of twenty-one from the raw base of one hundred twenty-one, giving one hundred. The untaxed total is the base of the first entry, one hundred, and the total with taxes is one hundred plus twenty-one.

records.name: The unit price after the discount
records.purpose: Reduces the stored unit price by the line's discount percentage before the engine sees it, so that every tax works on the price the customer is actually charged.

operands.name: unit price
operands.source: the base line
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: discount
operands.source: the base line
operands.constraints: zero by default

preconditions.condition: The discount is applied before the engine is called.
preconditions.otherwise: The engine would compute taxes on the undiscounted price; the engine only ever sees the discounted price.

procedure: Divide the discount percentage by one hundred.
Subtract the result from one.
Multiply the unit price by that factor.
Apply no rounding to the discounted price; the multiplication by the quantity happens on the full-precision value.
records.formula: price_unit_after_discount = price_unit × ( 1 − discount ÷ 100 )

rounding.what: Nothing.
rounding.method: Not applicable.
rounding.step: No rounding is applied to the discounted price; the first rounding of the line is the one applied to the raw base under the round-per-line method, or by the document-wide passes under the round-per-tax method.

result.name: unit price after discount
result.stored_or_displayed: Handed to the engine as the base line's unit price; also the value the custom-formula context exposes and the value whose sign a fixed tax reads.

edge_cases.case: The discount is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The factor is one and the price is unchanged.

edge_cases.case: The discount is one hundred percent.
edge_cases.outcome: The factor is zero, the price is zero and every percentage or division tax gives zero; a fixed tax still charges its per-unit amount, because it ignores the base.

edge_cases.case: The discounted price is rounded before being multiplied by the quantity.
edge_cases.outcome: The result diverges from the specification; the multiplication must happen on the full-precision value.

worked_examples.description: A price of twenty-one point five three with a ten percent discount, three units
worked_examples.narrative: One less ten divided by one hundred is zero point nine; twenty-one point five three multiplied by zero point nine is nineteen point three seven seven, which is not rounded; three times that is fifty-eight point one three one.

records.name: Converting a line amount into the company currency
records.purpose: Produces the company-currency twin of every amount of the tax details block, which is what the ledger balance is built from.

operands.name: amount in line currency
operands.source: the single-line computation
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: rate
operands.unit_or_currency: units of line currency per unit of company currency
operands.source: the base line
operands.constraints: one by default; may be zero

preconditions.condition: The rate is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: Every company-currency amount of the line is zero.

procedure: Immediately after the single-line computation, duplicate every amount into the company currency.
Because the rate counts units of line currency per unit of company currency, divide rather than multiply.
Return zero when the rate is zero.
Round each converted amount to the company currency immediately under the round-per-line method; leave it raw under the round-per-tax method, where the document-wide passes round it.
Convert the four totals and, for each tax entry, the base amount and the tax amount.
records.formula: amount_in_company_currency = amount_in_line_currency ÷ rate , or 0 when rate = 0

rounding.what: Each converted amount.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero.
rounding.step: Immediately after the conversion under the round-per-line method; in the document-wide passes under the round-per-tax method.

result.name: amount in company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the tax details block and posted as the balance of the journal items.

edge_cases.case: The rate is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: Every company-currency amount of the line is zero.

edge_cases.case: The rate is one.
edge_cases.outcome: The company-currency amounts equal the line-currency amounts.

edge_cases.case: The two currencies have different rounding steps.
edge_cases.outcome: Each currency is rounded and redistributed independently, so the allocations of a redistribution pass need not land on the same line in both currencies.

worked_examples.description: A line of twenty-one point five three at a rate of one point two five
worked_examples.narrative: Twenty-one point five three divided by one point two five is seventeen point two two four, which is left raw under the round-per-tax method and rounded to seventeen point two two under the round-per-line method.

records.name: The total with taxes of a non-deductible base line
records.purpose: Shows only the non-recoverable share of a partially deductible purchase, by dropping the reverse-charge halves of the line and removing their amounts from the total.

operands.name: result list of the base line
operands.source: the single-line computation
operands.constraints: may contain reverse-charge halves

operands.name: amount of each reverse-charge half
operands.source: the mirror records of the single-line computation
operands.constraints: negative

operands.name: deductible percentage of the originating document line
operands.source: the vendor bill line
operands.constraints: between zero and one hundred, enforced by the deductibility rule

preconditions.condition: The base line carries the special type marking it as non-deductible.
preconditions.otherwise: The result list and the total with taxes are left as the single-line computation produced them.

preconditions.condition: The originating document is a vendor bill.
preconditions.otherwise: The deductibility is refused with "Only vendor bills allow for deductibility of product/services."

procedure: Drop every reverse-charge half from the result list.
Subtract each dropped amount from the total with taxes.

For the host document, compute the non-deductible share of the originating line as the line subtotal multiplied by one less the deductible percentage divided by one hundred, rounded to the document currency, and the company-currency figure as the sign multiplied by that share divided by the rate, rounded to the company currency.
Create one base line of minus that share carrying the line's non-fixed taxes, and one base line of the total of those shares carrying no tax, which balances them.
records.formula: total_included = total_included − sum of the amounts of the dropped reverse-charge halves ; non_deductible_share_of_a_line = round_to_document_currency( line_subtotal × ( 1 − deductible_percentage ÷ 100 ) ) ; non_deductible_base_in_company_currency = round_to_company_currency( sign × that share ÷ rate )

rounding.what: The non-deductible share of each line, and its company-currency figure.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the document currency, and of the company currency for the converted figure.
rounding.method: Half away from zero.
rounding.step: The share is rounded before the extra base lines are built; the engine then rounds the resulting amounts as usual.

result.name: total with taxes of the non-deductible line, and the non-deductible tax amount
result.unit_or_currency: the document currency and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: The tax amount that falls out becomes a single journal item named "private part (taxes)"; the totals block reports it separately per tax group.

edge_cases.case: The deductible percentage is one hundred.
edge_cases.outcome: The non-deductible share is zero and no extra base line is produced.

edge_cases.case: The deductible percentage is outside the range zero to one hundred.
edge_cases.outcome: The document is refused with "The deductibility must be a value between 0 and 100."

edge_cases.case: The line carries a fixed tax.
edge_cases.outcome: Fixed taxes are excluded from the non-deductible base line, which carries only the line's non-fixed taxes.

worked_examples.description: A vendor bill line of one thousand with a twenty-one percent tax and a deductibility of forty percent
worked_examples.narrative: One less forty divided by one hundred is zero point six; one thousand multiplied by zero point six is six hundred. A base line of minus six hundred carrying the twenty-one percent tax and a balancing base line of six hundred carrying no tax are created; the tax that falls out of the first is minus one hundred twenty-six, which becomes the journal item named "private part (taxes)".

records.name: Smooth distribution of a rounding delta over weights
