preconditions.condition: The original tax item sits on an account that allows reconciliation.
preconditions.otherwise: No reconciliation is attempted; the transition account is required to allow reconciliation when a tax's exigibility is set to based on payment, with the message "The cash basis transition account needs to allow reconciliation."

preconditions.condition: The counterpart's amount does not round to zero.
preconditions.otherwise: It is skipped.

preconditions.condition: The items are not already reconciled.
preconditions.otherwise: They are skipped.

procedure: For every tax share whose original tax entry sits on a reconcilable account, reconcile the newly created counterpart item with that original tax entry.
Skip items that are already reconciled.
Skip counterparts whose amount rounded to zero.
Let the transition account empty as the document is paid, until the original tax item becomes fully reconciled.
records.formula: remaining on the transition account = original tax item amount − sum of the counterpart amounts reconciled against it ; the original tax item is fully reconciled when that remainder is zero at the currency's precision

rounding.what: The zero test on the counterpart's amount.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, inside the zero test.
rounding.step: Before the reconciliation is attempted.

result.name: the reconciliation between the counterpart and the original tax item
result.unit_or_currency: the document currency and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Recorded as a partial reconciliation; it may itself create an exchange difference entry when the two sides are in different currencies.

edge_cases.case: The counterpart's amount rounds to zero.
edge_cases.outcome: It is skipped and no reconciliation is created.

edge_cases.case: The two sides are in different currencies.
edge_cases.outcome: The reconciliation may create an exchange difference entry, recorded with its origin on the partial reconciliation so that undoing the reconciliation also undoes it.

edge_cases.case: The partial reconciliation is deleted.
edge_cases.outcome: Draft cash basis entries are deleted and posted ones are reversed and cancelled, the reversal carrying the reference "Reversal of: <the original entry's number>".

worked_examples.description: The transition account after the two instalments of the mandatory example
worked_examples.narrative: Eighty-four then one hundred twenty-six are matched against the two hundred ten, so the transition account reaches zero and the original tax item becomes fully reconciled.

records.name: Deriving the withholding lines of a payment
records.purpose: Produces, from the documents about to be paid, the list of amounts the payer retains and remits to the authorities on the payee's behalf.

operands.name: base lines of the documents about to be paid
operands.source: the documents
operands.constraints: rebuilt with withholding calculation enabled and no filter

operands.name: withholding tax base account of the company
operands.source: the company
operands.constraints: falls back to the base line's account when not set

operands.name: manual tax line name of the base line
operands.source: the base line
operands.constraints: the tax's name is used when absent

operands.name: existing withholding lines
operands.unit_or_currency: the payment currency and the company currency
operands.source: the payment
operands.constraints: grouped by the same key

preconditions.condition: The acting company owns at least one withholding tax matching the payment direction.
preconditions.otherwise: The withholding feature is not offered on the payment.

preconditions.condition: On the register-payment wizard, the wizard will create a single journal entry.
preconditions.otherwise: The feature is hidden: a wizard that cannot be edited, or one that will split into one payment per document, does not offer it.

procedure: Rebuild each base line with the withholding calculation enabled and no filter, then run the engine and the document-wide rounding on the rebuilt lines.

Aggregate the results by the name, the analytic distribution, the account, the tax, a skip indication and the currency, where the name is the base line's manual tax line name when it has one and the tax's name otherwise, the account is the company's withholding tax base account when set and the base line's account otherwise, and the skip indication is true for every tax that is not a withholding tax.
Ignore every group whose skip indication is true.
Compare with the withholding lines that already exist, grouped by the same key.
Keep the first and delete the others when more than one existing line shares a key.
Update an existing line's four source amounts: the base in document currency, the base in company currency, the tax in document currency negated and the tax in company currency negated.
Create a line with those four source amounts, the tax, the analytic distribution, the account, the name, the source tax and the source currency when none exists.
Delete the lines of a key that exists only among the existing lines.
records.formula: grouping key = ( name , analytic distribution , account , tax , skip indication , currency ) ; withholding_base_in_document_currency = the engine's base amount ; withholding_amount_in_document_currency = − the engine's tax amount ; the same in the company currency ; the negation turns the engine's negative tax amount into a positive amount withheld

rounding.what: The engine's amounts, through the ordinary document-wide rounding of the rebuilt lines.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the payment currency and of the company currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero.
rounding.step: Inside the engine run on the rebuilt lines, before the aggregation.

result.name: the withholding lines of the payment
result.unit_or_currency: the payment currency and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the payment and shown on the payment screen; each carries a base and a positive amount withheld.

edge_cases.case: A tax of the rebuilt line is not a withholding tax.
edge_cases.outcome: Its group carries the skip indication and is ignored.

edge_cases.case: A base amount is zero or negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The line is refused with "The base amount of a withholding tax line must be above 0."

edge_cases.case: The account chosen for a withholding line is a liquidity account of the owner's journal, an outstanding account of that journal's payment method lines, the owner's own outstanding account or the company's internal transfer account.
edge_cases.outcome: The line is refused with "The account "<the account's display name>" is not valid to use on withholding lines."

edge_cases.case: The user edits a line's amount by hand.
edge_cases.outcome: The override survives until the base changes again; editing the base rescales the amount by the same ratio as the original amounts.

worked_examples.description: Mandatory example eleven: a withholding tax of minus one percent on a base of one thousand
worked_examples.narrative: The engine computes minus ten on a base of one thousand; the negation turns it into a positive ten, and the base of one thousand was typed by hand, so no paid factor is applied and the amount is ten.

records.name: The net amount of a payment carrying withholding lines
records.purpose: The amount that actually reaches the bank once the withheld amounts have been retained, which is the figure the payment's liquidity item carries.

operands.name: payment amount
operands.source: the payment
operands.constraints: the debt being settled in full

operands.name: amount of each withholding line
operands.source: the withholding lines
operands.constraints: each is positive

preconditions.condition: The net amount is not negative.
preconditions.otherwise: Registering the payment is refused with "The withholding net amount cannot be negative."

procedure: Sum the amounts of the withholding lines.
Subtract that sum from the payment amount.
records.formula: withholding_net_amount = payment_amount − sum of the amounts of the withholding lines

rounding.what: Nothing new; the line amounts are already rounded.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the payment currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when each line amount was computed.
rounding.step: The subtraction is exact.

result.name: the withholding net amount
result.stored_or_displayed: Shown on the payment and carried by the liquidity journal item; the payment's own amount stays the full debt.

edge_cases.case: The sum of the withheld amounts exceeds the payment amount.
edge_cases.outcome: The net amount is negative and registering the payment is refused.

edge_cases.case: There is no withholding line.
edge_cases.outcome: The net amount equals the payment amount.

worked_examples.description: Mandatory example eleven: a payment of one thousand one hundred fifty with one withheld amount of ten
worked_examples.narrative: The customer's debt of one thousand one hundred fifty is settled in full, but only one thousand one hundred forty reaches the bank.

records.name: Turning the withholding lines into journal items
records.purpose: Builds, from each withholding line, the base line the engine consumes and the journal items the payment entry carries, so that the withheld amount and its base reach the tax return.

operands.name: withholding base of each line
operands.source: the withholding line
operands.constraints: strictly positive

operands.name: withholding amount of each line
operands.source: the withholding line
operands.constraints: positive

operands.name: conversion rate
operands.unit_or_currency: units of payment currency per unit of company currency
operands.source: the company's rate table at the payment date
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: direction of the payment
operands.source: the payment
operands.constraints: incoming or outgoing

operands.name: withholding certificate number
operands.source: the line, or the next value of the tax's withholding sequence
operands.constraints: every line must have one or a sequence before any value is drawn

preconditions.condition: Every line has either a number or a tax carrying a withholding sequence, checked before any sequence value is consumed.
preconditions.otherwise: The operation is refused with "Please enter the withholding number for the tax <the tax's name>", so that a failed attempt never burns a number.

preconditions.condition: Every line in the call belongs to the same payment.
preconditions.otherwise: The internal assertion "All withholding lines in self must have the same payment." fails, and on the register-payment wizard the corresponding assertion about the wizard.

procedure: Verify, before consuming any sequence value, that every line has either a number or a tax with a withholding sequence.
Draw the next value of the tax's withholding sequence for each line without a number.

Convert each line into a base line whose unit price is the line's withholding base, whose quantity is one, whose account is the line's account, whose computation key is the line's own identifier so that each line rounds independently, whose sign is plus one for an incoming payment and minus one for an outgoing one, and whose refund flag follows the rule of the entities document.
Set the base line's manual untaxed total in the payment currency to the withholding base and in the company currency to that base divided by the conversion rate, rounded to the company currency.

Set the base line's manual per-tax amounts for the line's tax: the base amount in the payment currency to the withholding base, the base amount in the company currency to that base divided by the conversion rate rounded to the company currency, the tax amount in the payment currency to the negated withholding amount, and the tax amount in the company currency to the negated withholding amount divided by the conversion rate, rounded to the company currency.
Run the engine, the document-wide rounding, the accounting derivation and the entry production on those base lines.
Emit one journal item per produced tax entry, with its amounts negated and the payment's partner, named with the words indicating a withholding tax followed by the tax's name.
Aggregate the base updates by their base grouping key extended with the tag set, summing the amounts and collecting the line names.

For each aggregate emit two journal items with the payment's partner: one carrying the aggregated amounts, no taxes and no tags, named with the words indicating a withholding base followed by the names; and one carrying the negated amounts, no analytic distribution, and keeping the taxes and the tags of the grouping key, named with the words indicating a withholding base counterpart followed by the names.
records.formula: conversion_rate = the rate from the company currency to the payment currency at the payment date ; sign = +1 for an incoming payment , −1 for an outgoing one ; price_unit = the line's withholding base ; quantity = 1 ; manual_total_excluded_currency = the withholding base ; manual_total_excluded = round_to_company_currency( withholding base ÷ conversion_rate ) ; manual base_amount_currency = the withholding base ; manual base_amount = round_to_company_currency( withholding base ÷ conversion_rate ) ; manual tax_amount_currency = − the withholding amount ; manual tax_amount = round_to_company_currency( − withholding amount ÷ conversion_rate )

rounding.what: Each company-currency manual amount.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero.
rounding.step: When the manual amounts are set, before the engine runs; because each line carries its own computation key, the lines round independently of each other.

result.name: the withholding journal items of the payment entry
result.unit_or_currency: the payment currency and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Added to the payment's own journal entry, not to a separate one.

edge_cases.case: A line has no number and its tax has no withholding sequence.
edge_cases.outcome: The operation is refused before any sequence value is drawn.

edge_cases.case: Two withholding lines share a base grouping key and a tag set.
edge_cases.outcome: Their base updates are aggregated into one pair of items whose names list both line names.

edge_cases.case: Each line carries its own computation key.
edge_cases.outcome: The redistribution passes never move a unit of the last decimal place from one withholding line to another.

worked_examples.description: Mandatory example eleven: a payment of one thousand one hundred fifty with a withheld amount of ten
worked_examples.narrative: The liquidity item is a debit of one thousand one hundred forty on the outstanding receipts account, the receivable is credited one thousand one hundred fifty, the withholding tax item debits ten on the withholding tax credit account, and the two base items of one thousand cancel on the withholding base account, existing only so that the base reaches the tax return through the base tags of the withholding tax's distribution.

records.name: The paid factor of a withholding line derived from the documents
records.purpose: The instalment variant of a withholding: when the line is derived from the documents rather than typed by hand, the base and the amount are scaled by the share of the batch being paid.

operands.name: full amount still to pay for the batch
operands.source: the documents about to be paid
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: total of the documents
operands.source: the documents about to be paid
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: instalment amount
operands.source: the payment being registered
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: original base amount
operands.source: the derivation of the withholding lines
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: original tax amount
operands.source: the derivation of the withholding lines
operands.constraints: the negated engine amount

preconditions.condition: The withholding line was derived from the documents rather than typed by hand.
preconditions.otherwise: No paid factor applies and the base is used as typed.

procedure: Compute the split factor as the full amount still to pay for the batch divided by the total of the documents.
Compute the paid factor as the instalment amount divided by the full amount still to pay, multiplied by the split factor.
Multiply the original base amount by the paid factor and round to the payment currency to obtain the line's base.
Derive the amount as the original tax amount multiplied by the line's base and divided by the original base amount, rounded to the payment currency.
Subtract the amounts of the withholding lines from the instalment to obtain the net amount.
records.formula: split_factor = full_amount ÷ moves_total ; percentage_paid_factor = instalment ÷ full_amount × split_factor ; base_amount = round( original_base_amount × percentage_paid_factor ) ; amount = round( original_tax_amount × base_amount ÷ original_base_amount ) ; withholding_net_amount = instalment − sum of the amounts

rounding.what: The line's base and the line's amount.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the payment currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero.
rounding.step: The base is rounded first and the amount is then derived from the rounded base, so that the ratio between the two stays the ratio of the original amounts.

result.name: the base and the amount of the withholding line, and the net amount
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the withholding line and shown on the payment.

edge_cases.case: The whole batch is paid at once.
edge_cases.outcome: The paid factor is one and the base and the amount are the originals.

edge_cases.case: The user edits the base by hand.
edge_cases.outcome: The amount is rescaled by the same ratio as the original amounts.

edge_cases.case: The user edits the amount by hand.
edge_cases.outcome: The override survives until the base changes again.

worked_examples.description: Mandatory example eleven with an instalment: half of an invoice of one thousand one hundred fifty
worked_examples.narrative: The split factor is one; the paid factor is five hundred seventy-five divided by one thousand one hundred fifty, that is zero point five. The base becomes five hundred and the amount ten multiplied by five hundred divided by one thousand, that is five; the net amount is five hundred seventy.

records.name: Whether a tax can be discounted
records.purpose: Excludes per-unit charges from every proportional operation, because scaling them by a discount percentage would misstate them.

operands.name: computation kind of the tax
operands.source: the tax
operands.constraints: fixed amount, percentage, division, custom formula or group of taxes

preconditions.condition: The caller is performing a proportional operation such as a global discount or a down payment.
preconditions.otherwise: The test is not consulted.

procedure: Return false when the tax's computation kind is the fixed amount kind or the custom formula kind.
Return true otherwise.
records.formula: can_be_discounted( tax ) = tax.amount_type is neither `fixed` nor `code`

rounding.what: Nothing.
rounding.method: Not applicable.
rounding.step: The test is consulted before the proportional operation runs.

result.name: the discountable indication
result.stored_or_displayed: Used to decide which taxes a global discount drops and which a down payment wraps into the base.

edge_cases.case: The tax is a fixed amount.
edge_cases.outcome: It cannot be discounted; a global discount drops it and a down payment wraps it into the base.

edge_cases.case: The tax is a custom formula.
edge_cases.outcome: The same, because it too is a per-unit charge.

edge_cases.case: The tax is a percentage or a division tax.
edge_cases.outcome: It can be discounted and is scaled with the rest.

worked_examples.description: A line carrying a fixed levy and a percentage tax
worked_examples.narrative: The percentage tax is scaled by the operation; the fixed levy is dropped by a global discount or wrapped into the base by a down payment.

records.name: Splitting a base line by weights
records.purpose: Divides one base line into several such that computing taxes on the pieces gives exactly the same result as on the whole.

operands.name: weights
operands.source: the caller
operands.constraints: one per piece

operands.name: raw amounts of the whole
operands.unit_or_currency: the line currency and the company currency
operands.source: the tax details block
operands.constraints: the four totals and each tax entry's four raw amounts

operands.name: rounded amounts of the whole
operands.unit_or_currency: the line currency and the company currency
operands.source: the tax details block
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: unit price of the whole
operands.source: the base line
operands.constraints: none

preconditions.condition: At least one weight is supplied.
preconditions.otherwise: There is nothing to split into.

procedure: Normalise the weights as the smooth distribution does: absolute value, original position kept, sorted by absolute value descending, divided by the sum of the absolute values, and one divided by the number of weights when that sum is zero.
Multiply every raw amount of the whole, that is the four totals and each tax entry's four raw amounts, by the normalised weight of the piece.

Distribute every rounded amount by the smooth distribution, taking the delta to distribute as the whole's rounded amount and the weights as the pieces' weights, which guarantees that the pieces add back exactly to the whole.
Set each piece's total with taxes to its untaxed total plus the sum of its tax amounts.
Build each piece's base line with a unit price equal to the whole's unit price multiplied by the normalised weight, and attach the piece's tax details.
records.formula: normalised_weight_i = | weight_i | ÷ sum of | weight_j | , or 1 ÷ number_of_weights when that sum is 0 ; raw amount of piece i = raw amount of the whole × normalised_weight_i ; rounded amounts of the pieces = the smooth distribution of the whole's rounded amount over the pieces' weights ; total_included of piece i = total_excluded of piece i + sum of its tax amounts ; unit price of piece i = unit price of the whole × normalised_weight_i

rounding.what: The rounded amounts of the pieces.
rounding.precision: Whole units of the last decimal place of the currency.
rounding.method: The smooth distribution's allocation, which uses the host nearest-integer rule and then hands out the leftover one unit at a time.
rounding.step: The raw amounts are scaled without rounding; only the rounded amounts go through the distribution, which is what makes the pieces add back exactly.

result.name: the pieces, each a complete base line with its own tax details
result.unit_or_currency: the line currency and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Handed back to the caller; used by the global discount and the down payment.

edge_cases.case: The weights sum to zero.
edge_cases.outcome: Every normalised weight is one divided by the number of pieces.

edge_cases.case: A rounded amount cannot be divided evenly.
edge_cases.outcome: The smooth distribution places the leftover units, so the pieces still add back to the whole.

edge_cases.case: One weight is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: That piece receives a raw amount of zero and, unless a leftover unit falls on it, a rounded amount of zero.

worked_examples.description: A line of one hundred untaxed with twenty-one of tax split into two equal pieces
worked_examples.narrative: Each normalised weight is one half; the raw amounts halve exactly and the distribution of the rounded amounts gives fifty and ten point five zero to each piece, which add back to the whole.

records.name: Merging two tax details blocks
records.purpose: Combines the results of two base lines into one, keeping the merged base meaningful for a tax whose base is an artefact, such as a fixed levy.

operands.name: the four totals and the two deltas of each block
operands.unit_or_currency: the line currency and the company currency
operands.source: the two tax details blocks
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: the eight amounts of each tax entry
operands.unit_or_currency: the line currency and the company currency
operands.source: the two blocks
operands.constraints: raw and rounded, base and tax, in both currencies

operands.name: the taxes present in the first block but absent from the second
operands.source: the two blocks
operands.constraints: typically fixed taxes

preconditions.condition: The two blocks belong to base lines that carry the same currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The merge would add amounts of different currencies.

procedure: Add the four totals of the two blocks and add the two deltas.
Merge the tax entries by tax, adding all eight amounts.

For every tax present in the first block but absent from the second, add the second block's untaxed totals to that tax's base amounts and the second block's untaxed deltas to its rounded base amounts, so that the merged base stays meaningful.
records.formula: merged total = total of the first block + total of the second block , for each of the four totals and the two deltas ; merged tax entry amounts = the sum of the two entries' eight amounts , per tax ; for a tax present only in the first block : merged base amounts = base amounts of the first block + the second block's untaxed totals , and merged rounded base amounts = rounded base amounts + the second block's untaxed deltas

rounding.what: Nothing; the merge only adds already-computed amounts.
rounding.precision: The amounts keep the precision they already had.
rounding.method: Not applicable.
rounding.step: No rounding step is involved.

result.name: the merged tax details block
result.unit_or_currency: the line currency and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Attached to the reduced base line the caller builds.

edge_cases.case: A fixed tax appears only in the first block.
edge_cases.outcome: Its base is an artefact, so the second block's untaxed totals are added to it and the merged base still describes the whole amount the levy was charged on.

edge_cases.case: A tax appears in both blocks.
edge_cases.outcome: Its eight amounts are added pairwise.

edge_cases.case: A tax appears only in the second block.
edge_cases.outcome: It is carried over as it stands; no correction is applied, because the correction exists for taxes of the first block.

worked_examples.description: Merging a line of one hundred carrying a fixed levy with a line of fifty carrying no tax
worked_examples.narrative: The untaxed totals add to one hundred fifty. The levy is present only in the first block, so the second block's untaxed total of fifty is added to its base, which becomes one hundred fifty; its amount is untouched, because a fixed levy does not depend on the base.

records.name: Reducing many base lines to few
records.purpose: Minimises the number of lines a discount or a down payment has to create, without changing any total.

operands.name: quantity and discounted unit price of each base line
operands.unit_or_currency: the line's unit of measure and the line currency
operands.source: the base lines
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: set of taxes of each base line
operands.source: the base lines
operands.constraints: the grouping key, extended by the caller's own keys

operands.name: tax details block of each base line
operands.unit_or_currency: the line currency and the company currency
operands.source: the engine
operands.constraints: merged within a group

preconditions.condition: Every line of a group carries the same set of taxes and the same caller-supplied grouping keys.
preconditions.otherwise: The lines fall into different groups and are not combined.

procedure: Turn each base line into an equivalent line of quantity one whose unit price is the quantity multiplied by the discounted unit price and whose discount is zero.
Group the resulting lines by the set of taxes, extended by the caller's own grouping keys.
Within a group, add the unit prices and merge the tax details.
Drop the groups whose unit price is zero at the currency's precision.
Recompute the analytic distribution of each group as a weighted average of its members' distributions, weighted by each member's raw untaxed total.
records.formula: unit price of the equivalent line = quantity × discounted unit price , quantity = 1 , discount = 0 ; unit price of a group = sum of the members' unit prices ; a group is dropped when is_zero( its unit price , the currency step )

rounding.what: The zero test on a group's unit price.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the line currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, inside the zero test.
rounding.step: After the unit prices are added and before the group is kept.

result.name: the reduced base lines
result.stored_or_displayed: Handed to the caller, which scales them and runs the engine on the result.

edge_cases.case: A group's unit price is zero at the currency's precision.
edge_cases.outcome: The group is dropped, because a line of zero would carry no amount.

edge_cases.case: Two lines carry the same taxes but different analytic distributions.
edge_cases.outcome: They are still combined and the distribution becomes the weighted average.

edge_cases.case: A line carries a discount.
edge_cases.outcome: The equivalent line folds the discount into the unit price and sets the discount to zero.

worked_examples.description: Two lines carrying the same tax, one of three units at ten and one of two units at five
worked_examples.narrative: Each line becomes a line of quantity one at thirty and at ten; they share a tax set, so they combine into a single line of quantity one at forty.

records.name: The weighted-average analytic distribution of a reduced group
records.purpose: Preserves the analytic split of the lines a reduction combines, so that the reduced line charges each analytic account the share it actually bore.

operands.name: analytic percentage of each member for an account
operands.source: the member's analytic distribution
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: raw untaxed total of each member
operands.source: the tax details block
operands.constraints: may be negative

preconditions.condition: The sum of the members' raw untaxed totals is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The new percentage is one hundred.

procedure: For each analytic account, compute its weight as the sum over the members of the member's percentage for that account multiplied by the member's raw untaxed total and divided by one hundred.
Multiply that weight by one hundred and divide by the sum of the members' raw untaxed totals to obtain the new percentage.
Set the new percentage to one hundred when the sum of the members' raw untaxed totals is zero.
records.formula: weight_of_account = sum over the members of ( member_distribution_percentage × member_raw_untaxed ÷ 100 ) ; new_percentage = weight_of_account × 100 ÷ sum of member_raw_untaxed ; new_percentage = 100 when the sum of the members' raw untaxed totals is zero

rounding.what: Nothing at this step; the percentage is kept at full precision.
rounding.precision: Analytic percentages are handled with two decimal places when they are stored.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, when the percentage is stored.
rounding.step: The weighted average is computed on raw untaxed totals, before any rounding.

result.name: the analytic percentage of each account on the reduced line
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as the reduced line's analytic distribution and carried onto the journal items it produces.

edge_cases.case: One member has a negative raw untaxed total.
edge_cases.outcome: It reduces the weight of the accounts it charges, and the resulting percentage may exceed one hundred.

edge_cases.case: The members' raw untaxed totals cancel.
edge_cases.outcome: The new percentage is one hundred.

edge_cases.case: Every member charges the same account at one hundred percent.
edge_cases.outcome: The new percentage is one hundred.

worked_examples.description: A line of one thousand at one hundred percent on an account and a line of minus one hundred at fifty percent on the same account
worked_examples.narrative: One thousand times one plus minus one hundred times zero point five is nine hundred fifty; divided by nine hundred and multiplied by one hundred that is one hundred five point five five five recurring, which is one hundred five point five six percent at two decimal places.

records.name: Reaching a target amount expressed as a fixed amount
records.purpose: The first variant of the operation behind a global discount and a down payment: the caller names an amount and the document is scaled so that the new lines total exactly that amount.

operands.name: base lines
operands.source: the document
operands.constraints: already computed

operands.name: requested amount
operands.source: the caller
operands.constraints: may be negative

operands.name: current grand total
operands.unit_or_currency: the line currency and the company currency
operands.source: the engine
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: current base and tax amount per tax
operands.unit_or_currency: the line currency and the company currency
operands.source: the engine
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: rate
operands.unit_or_currency: units of line currency per unit of company currency
operands.source: the base lines
operands.constraints: none

preconditions.condition: The current grand total in the line currency is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The derived percentage is zero and no amount can be scaled.

procedure: Compute the current grand total in both currencies and the current base and tax amount per tax.
Set the sign to minus one when the requested amount is negative and plus one otherwise.
Set the percentage to the absolute requested amount divided by the current grand total in the line currency, and to zero when that total is zero.
Set the target grand total in the line currency to the requested amount rounded to the line currency, and in the company currency to that value divided by the rate, rounded to the company currency.

Set the target base and tax amount of each tax to the current ones multiplied by the sign and the percentage, rounded, and the target untaxed total to the target grand total less the sum of the target tax amounts.
Reduce the lines, scale each reduced line's unit price by the sign and the percentage, and run the engine and the document-wide rounding on the result.

Sort the new lines by whether they carry a special type and then by untaxed total descending, and, per tax and per currency, distribute the difference between the target and the achieved tax amount and likewise for the base amount, using the smooth distribution weighted by each entry's share.
Distribute the remaining difference on the untaxed totals into the lines' untaxed deltas and, in the line currency, also into their unit prices.
Freeze the result into manual amounts, so that recomputing the document cannot move it.
records.formula: sign = −1 when the requested amount is negative , +1 otherwise ; percentage = | amount | ÷ current_total_in_line_currency , 0 when that total is 0 ; target_total_currency = round_to_line_currency( amount ) ; target_total = round_to_company_currency( target_total_currency ÷ rate ) ; target base and tax amount of each tax = round( current amount × sign × percentage ) ; target_total_excluded = target_total − sum of the target tax amounts

rounding.what: The target grand total in each currency and each target base and tax amount.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the line currency and of the company currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero.
rounding.step: The targets are rounded before the lines are scaled; the differences between the targets and what the engine achieves are then distributed and finally frozen.

result.name: the scaled base lines and their frozen manual amounts
result.unit_or_currency: the line currency and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on the document as the discount or the down payment lines.

edge_cases.case: The current grand total is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The percentage is zero and no line carries an amount.

edge_cases.case: A global discount calls the operation.
edge_cases.outcome: It passes the negated amount, after dropping every non-discountable tax.

edge_cases.case: A down payment calls the operation.
edge_cases.outcome: It passes the amount as given, after wrapping every non-discountable tax into the base.

edge_cases.case: The result is not frozen.
edge_cases.outcome: A later recomputation moves the total off the requested amount, which is exactly what the freeze prevents.

worked_examples.description: A global discount of one hundred twenty-one on a document totalling one thousand two hundred ten with a twenty-one percent tax
worked_examples.narrative: The percentage is one hundred twenty-one divided by one thousand two hundred ten, that is zero point one; the target grand total is minus one hundred twenty-one, the target tax minus twenty-one and the target untaxed total minus one hundred.

records.name: Reaching a target amount expressed as a percentage
records.purpose: The second variant of the same operation: the caller names a percentage of the current total and the document is scaled to it.

operands.name: base lines
operands.source: the document
operands.constraints: already computed

operands.name: requested percentage
operands.source: the caller
operands.constraints: may be negative

operands.name: current grand total
operands.unit_or_currency: the line currency and the company currency
operands.source: the engine
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: current base and tax amount per tax
operands.unit_or_currency: the line currency and the company currency
operands.source: the engine
operands.constraints: none

preconditions.condition: The current grand total has been computed in both currencies.
preconditions.otherwise: There is nothing to take a percentage of.

procedure: Compute the current grand total in both currencies and the current base and tax amount per tax.
Set the sign to minus one when the requested amount is negative and plus one otherwise.
Set the percentage to the absolute requested amount divided by one hundred.

Set the target grand total in the line currency to the current total in that currency multiplied by the sign and the percentage, rounded to the line currency, and in the company currency to the current company total multiplied by the sign and the percentage, rounded to the company currency.

Set the target base and tax amount of each tax to the current ones multiplied by the sign and the percentage, rounded, and the target untaxed total to the target grand total less the sum of the target tax amounts.
Reduce the lines, scale each reduced line's unit price by the sign and the percentage, and run the engine and the document-wide rounding.
Distribute the differences per tax and per currency, then the remaining untaxed difference into the deltas and the unit prices, and freeze the result into manual amounts.
records.formula: sign = −1 when the requested amount is negative , +1 otherwise ; percentage = | amount | ÷ 100 ; target_total_currency = round_to_line_currency( current_total_currency × sign × percentage ) ; target_total = round_to_company_currency( current_total × sign × percentage ) ; target base and tax amount of each tax = round( current amount × sign × percentage ) ; target_total_excluded = target_total − sum of the target tax amounts

rounding.what: The two target grand totals and each target base and tax amount.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the line currency and of the company currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero.
rounding.step: Each currency's target is computed from that currency's current total, so the two are rounded independently rather than one being converted from the other.

result.name: the scaled base lines and their frozen manual amounts
result.unit_or_currency: the line currency and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on the document as the discount or the down payment lines.

edge_cases.case: The requested percentage is one hundred.
edge_cases.outcome: The target equals the current total and the operation reproduces the document.

edge_cases.case: The requested percentage is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The sign is minus one and the target amounts are the negated share.

edge_cases.case: The company-currency target is derived by converting the line-currency target.
edge_cases.outcome: That is not what the specification says: each currency's target is computed from its own current total.

worked_examples.description: A down payment of thirty percent of a document totalling one thousand two hundred ten with a twenty-one percent tax
worked_examples.narrative: Thirty percent of one thousand two hundred ten is three hundred sixty-three, of which sixty-three is tax and three hundred the untaxed amount.

records.name: Dispatching taxes into separate base lines
records.purpose: Removes some taxes from a proportional operation without losing their amounts, by moving those amounts into extra base lines that carry no tax.

operands.name: base lines
operands.source: the document
operands.constraints: already computed

operands.name: taxes to keep and taxes to exclude
operands.source: the caller
operands.constraints: a partition of each line's taxes

operands.name: tax amounts of the excluded taxes
operands.unit_or_currency: the line currency and the company currency
operands.source: the tax details block
operands.constraints: none

preconditions.condition: The partition covers every tax of the line.
preconditions.otherwise: An amount would be lost and the grand total would change.

procedure: Partition each base line's taxes into the taxes to keep and the taxes to exclude.
Leave on the original line the taxes to keep.
Move the amounts of the excluded taxes into new base lines that carry no tax at all.
Verify that the resulting set has the same grand total as the original, so that it can be scaled safely.
Use the symmetric helpers to squash those extra lines back, and to dispatch the global discount lines and the return-of-merchandise lines the same way.
records.formula: grand total of the dispatched set = grand total of the original set ; each excluded tax amount becomes the untaxed total of a new base line carrying no tax

rounding.what: Nothing new; the amounts moved are already rounded.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the line currency and of the company currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied earlier.
rounding.step: The move is exact, which is why the grand total is preserved.

result.name: the dispatched base lines
result.unit_or_currency: the line currency and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Handed to the proportional operation; the squashing helper folds them back afterwards.

edge_cases.case: A down payment must not scale a fixed levy.
edge_cases.outcome: The levy is excluded and its amount is moved into a base line carrying no tax, so the scaling leaves it intact while the grand total stays right.

edge_cases.case: No tax is excluded.
edge_cases.outcome: No extra line is created and the set is unchanged.

worked_examples.description: A line of one hundred five untaxed carrying a fixed levy of zero point three five and a twenty percent tax, with the levy excluded
worked_examples.narrative: The levy's zero point three five moves into a base line carrying no tax; the grand total of one hundred twenty-six point three five is unchanged and the remaining set can be scaled safely.

records.name: Pairing a tax journal item with the base journal items it was computed on
records.purpose: Rebuilds, for an already posted entry, which base item contributed to which tax item, a link the entry does not store.

operands.name: tax item
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency and the document currency
operands.source: the posted entry
operands.constraints: carries a distribution line

operands.name: candidate base item
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency and the document currency
operands.source: the same entry
operands.constraints: must carry no distribution line

operands.name: originator tax and its distribution line
operands.source: the tax item
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: balance, partner, currency, account and analytic distribution of both items
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency and not applicable
operands.source: the posted items
operands.constraints: compared by the nine conditions

preconditions.condition: The entry is posted.
preconditions.otherwise: The mapping is not meaningful; the engine computes the link directly on a draft document.

procedure: Pair a tax item with a base item of the same entry only when the base item is not itself a tax item, that is when it carries no distribution line.
Require the base item to carry, among its base taxes, the tax recorded as the tax item's originator group when there is one, and the tax item's originator tax otherwise.

Require that either the entry is not a miscellaneous entry, or the originator tax is exigible on payment and has a transition account, or the sign of the tax item's balance equals the sign of the base item's balance multiplied by the tax's rate and by the distribution line's factor.
Require the two partners to be equal, treating the absence of a partner as equal to the absence of a partner.
Require the two currencies to be equal.

Require that either the distribution line's account, falling back to the base item's own account, equals the tax item's account, or the originator tax is exigible on payment and has a transition account.

Require that either the originator tax is not analytic and the distribution line is used in the tax settlement, or both items have no analytic distribution, or the two analytic distributions are equal.
Apply the tail test in addition when the originator tax affects the base of subsequent taxes.
Emit one row per surviving pair, whose base amount is the base item's own balance and whose base amount in document currency is the base item's own amount in document currency.
records.formula: a pair ( tax item T , base item B ) survives when all nine conditions hold ; row.base_amount = B.balance ; row.base_amount_in_document_currency = B.amount in document currency

rounding.what: Nothing at this step; the balances are taken as posted.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency and of the document currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when the items were written.
rounding.step: The allocation of the tax amounts, which does round, happens in a later step.

result.name: the raw rows of the mapping, each carrying a base amount
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency and the document currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Consumed by reports, audits and structured document formats; never stored.

edge_cases.case: The entry is a miscellaneous entry.
edge_cases.outcome: The sign test is the only evidence of which side of the transaction a line belongs to, so it is applied unless the tax is exigible on payment and has a transition account.

edge_cases.case: The tax is exigible on payment and has a transition account.
edge_cases.outcome: The sign test and the account test are both waived, because the tax item sits on the transition account rather than on the distribution line's account.

edge_cases.case: A tax item is paired with no base item at all.
edge_cases.outcome: The fallback mapping adds an approximate pairing, unless the caller switched it off, in which case the orphan tax item produces no row.

worked_examples.description: The illustrating entry: three base items and four tax items

base_taxes: the ten percent tax that affects the base
the ten percent tax that affects the base
the ten percent tax that affects the base

tax_1.originator: the ten percent tax that affects the base

tax_3.originator: the ten percent tax that affects the base

worked_examples.narrative: Six pairs survive. The tail test keeps the first tax item with the first base item only, and the third tax item with the second and third base items only.

records.name: The tail test for a tax that affects the base
records.purpose: Restricts a base-affecting tax's item to the base items that carry exactly the same downstream taxes, so that its amount is not attributed to a base it never swelled.

operands.name: affecting-tax list of the base item
operands.source: the base item's taxes, with every Group of Taxes expanded into its children, every tax that does not accept being affected by previous taxes dropped, and the rest sorted by sequence and identifier
operands.constraints: ordered

operands.name: affecting-tax list of the tax item
operands.source: the tax item's own base taxes, built the same way
operands.constraints: ordered

operands.name: originator tax of the tax item
operands.source: the tax item
operands.constraints: affects the base of subsequent taxes

preconditions.condition: The originator tax affects the base of subsequent taxes.
preconditions.otherwise: The test does not apply and the eight other conditions decide the pairing.

procedure: Build the affecting-tax list of a journal item: expand every Group of Taxes into its children, drop every tax that does not accept being affected by previous taxes, and sort what remains by sequence and then by identifier.
Take the tail of the base item's list, that is its last entries, one more than the length of the tax item's own list.
Keep the pair when that tail equals the tax item's originator tax followed by the tax item's own affecting-tax list.
records.formula: tail = the affecting-tax list of B restricted to its last ( 1 + length of the affecting-tax list of T ) entries ; the pair survives when tail = [ T's originator tax ] followed by T's own affecting-tax list

rounding.what: Nothing.
rounding.method: Not applicable.
rounding.step: The test compares ordered lists of taxes.

result.name: the survival indication of the pair
result.stored_or_displayed: Used inside the mapping algorithm.

edge_cases.case: The tax item carries no base tax of its own.
edge_cases.outcome: The required tail is the originator tax alone, so the base item's list must end with it.

edge_cases.case: Two base items carry the same affecting tax but different downstream taxes.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the one whose tail matches survives, which is exactly why the test exists.

edge_cases.case: A Group of Taxes appears in a list.
edge_cases.outcome: It is expanded into its children before the comparison.

worked_examples.description: The illustrating entry: the first tax item against the three base items

inputs.tax_item_originator: the ten percent tax that affects the base
base_1_affecting_list: the ten percent tax that affects the base
base_2_affecting_list: the ten percent tax that affects the base
base_3_affecting_list: the ten percent tax that affects the base

required_tail: the ten percent tax that affects the base

worked_examples.narrative: The tax item's own list has one entry, so the tail is the last two entries of each base item's list. Only the first base item's tail equals the affecting tax followed by the twenty percent tax.

records.name: The extra base a base-affecting tax contributes
records.purpose: Adds the rows that record a tax item as part of a later tax's base, allocating that tax item's whole amount over the base items it was itself computed on.

operands.name: amount of the source tax item
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency and the document currency
operands.source: the posted tax item whose originator tax affects the base
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: contribution of each base item
operands.source: the absolute quantity carrying the sign of the balance when the tax is fixed, and the balance otherwise
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: ordering
operands.source: the originator tax of the later tax item, then the base item's identifier
operands.constraints: fixes the running total

preconditions.condition: The source tax item's originator tax affects the base of subsequent taxes.
preconditions.otherwise: No extra base row is produced for it.

preconditions.condition: The later tax item shares a base item with the source and its originator tax is one of the source's own base taxes.
preconditions.otherwise: The pair is not considered.

preconditions.condition: The total of the contributions is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: Every extra base amount is zero.

procedure: Enumerate the base items that the raw mapping paired with the source tax item.
Order them by the originator tax of the later tax item, then by the base item's identifier.
Compute each base item's contribution as the absolute quantity carrying the sign of the balance when the tax is a fixed one, and as the balance otherwise.
Build the running sum of the contributions over that ordering, and the total over every base item.

Compute the allocation up to each base item as the source's balance multiplied by the absolute running sum, divided by the total, carrying the sign of the running sum, and rounded to the company currency; take it as zero when the total is zero.
Take each base item's extra base as the allocation up to it less the allocation up to the previous one, with zero for the first.
Compute the same independently in the document currency.
Emit one row per base item, carrying that extra base amount, the later tax item as the tax item, the base item as the base item and the source tax item as the source item.
records.formula: contribution_of_B = | B.quantity | carrying the sign of B's balance when the tax is fixed , B.balance otherwise ; cumulated( B ) = the running sum of contribution over the ordering ; total = the sum over every B ; allocated_up_to( B ) = round_to_company_currency( sign( cumulated(B) ) × S.balance × | cumulated(B) | ÷ total ) ; extra_base_for( B ) = allocated_up_to( B ) − allocated_up_to( the previous B ) , with zero for the first and the whole expression zero when the total is zero

rounding.what: The cumulative allocation, once per base item.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency, and separately of the document currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero.
rounding.step: The running total is rounded and the differences are taken, so the last base item absorbs whatever the earlier roundings left over and the allocations always add back to the source's amount exactly.

result.name: the extra base rows
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency and the document currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Added to the mapping; each names the source tax item as the source.

edge_cases.case: The total of the contributions is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: Every extra base amount is zero.

edge_cases.case: The affecting tax is a fixed one.
edge_cases.outcome: The contribution is the absolute quantity carrying the sign of the balance, not the balance, because a fixed levy is charged per unit.

edge_cases.case: The allocations are computed by rounding each share independently.
edge_cases.outcome: They no longer add back to the source's amount; the running-total technique is what guarantees they do.

worked_examples.description: The illustrating entry: the extra base contributed by the first and the third tax items
worked_examples.narrative: The one hundred of the first tax item goes entirely to the single base item it was computed on. The five hundred of the third tax item is split two fifths and three fifths, because the second and third base items contribute two thousand and three thousand: the running total gives two hundred then five hundred, so the differences are two hundred and three hundred.

records.name: The fallback mapping for an orphan tax journal item
records.purpose: Gives an approximate base for a tax item that the strict pairing left unmatched, which happens when the configuration changed after the entry was posted or when the entry was imported.

operands.name: orphan tax item
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency and the document currency
operands.source: the posted entry
operands.constraints: paired with no base item by the raw mapping

operands.name: base items of the same entry and the same currency
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency and the document currency
operands.source: the posted entry
operands.constraints: must carry the tax item's originator group or originator tax among their base taxes

operands.name: caller's choice
operands.source: the caller
operands.constraints: the fallback may be switched off

preconditions.condition: The raw mapping paired the tax item with no base item at all.
preconditions.otherwise: The fallback is not applied to it.

preconditions.condition: The caller left the fallback switched on.
preconditions.otherwise: The orphan tax item simply produces no row.

procedure: Pair the orphan tax item with every base item of the same entry and the same currency that carries, among its base taxes, the tax item's originator group or its originator tax.
Apply no other condition: neither the sign test, nor the account test, nor the analytic test, nor the tail test.
Give each row the base item's whole balance as its base amount.
records.formula: for an orphan tax item T : rows = one row per base item B of the same entry and the same currency whose base taxes contain T's originator group or T's originator tax ; row.base_amount = B.balance

rounding.what: Nothing at this step; the balances are taken as posted.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency and of the document currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when the items were written.
rounding.step: The tax amounts of these rows are allocated by the later step, which does round.

result.name: the fallback rows
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency and the document currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Added to the mapping; they are approximate and marked as such by their origin.

edge_cases.case: The caller switched the fallback off.
edge_cases.outcome: The orphan tax item produces no row at all.

edge_cases.case: No base item of the entry carries the originator tax.
edge_cases.outcome: The fallback finds nothing and the tax item still produces no row.

edge_cases.case: Several base items qualify.
edge_cases.outcome: Each produces a row carrying its whole balance; the tax amount is then allocated over them by the running-total technique.

worked_examples.description: A tax item of two hundred ten whose account no longer matches any base item's
worked_examples.narrative: The strict pairing found nothing, so the single base item carrying the tax is paired with the orphan and the row carries the base item's whole balance of minus one thousand.

records.name: Allocating the tax amount over the rows of a tax journal item
records.purpose: Gives every row of the mapping its share of the tax item's amount, in a way that always adds back to the item's balance exactly.

operands.name: balance of the tax item
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency and the document currency
operands.source: the posted tax item
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: contribution of each row
operands.source: the absolute quantity of the base item carrying the sign of its balance when the tax is fixed, and the row's own base amount otherwise
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: ordering of the rows
operands.source: the originator tax, then the base item's identifier, then the source item's identifier
operands.constraints: fixes the running total

preconditions.condition: The total of the contributions of a tax item's rows is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: Every allocated tax amount is zero.

procedure: Order the rows of a tax item by its originator tax, then by the base item's identifier, then by the source item's identifier.
Compute each row's contribution as the absolute quantity of the base item carrying the sign of its balance when the tax is a fixed one, and as the row's own base amount otherwise.
Build the running sum of the contributions over that ordering and the total over every row of the tax item.

Compute the allocation up to each row as the tax item's balance multiplied by the absolute running sum, divided by the total, carrying the sign of the running sum, and rounded to the company currency.
Take each row's tax amount as the allocation up to it less the allocation up to the previous row, with zero for the first row and the whole expression zero when the total is zero.
Compute the same independently in the document currency.
records.formula: contribution = | B.quantity | carrying the sign of B's balance when the tax is fixed , the row's own base amount otherwise ; cumulated = the running sum of contribution over the ordering ; total = the sum over every row of the tax item ; allocated_up_to = round_to_company_currency( sign( cumulated ) × T.balance × | cumulated | ÷ total ) ; tax_amount = allocated_up_to − the previous row's allocated_up_to , with zero for the first row and the whole expression zero when the total is zero

rounding.what: The cumulative allocation, once per row.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency, and separately of the document currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero.
rounding.step: The running total is rounded and the differences are taken, so the last row absorbs whatever the earlier roundings left over and the allocations always add back to the tax item's balance exactly.

result.name: the tax amount of each row
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency and the document currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Read by reports, audits and structured document formats; the row also carries its identifier, the three items, the display kind, the tax, the originator group of taxes, the distribution line, the base account, the exigible indication and the company and currency information.

edge_cases.case: The total of the contributions is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: Every allocated tax amount is zero.

edge_cases.case: Each share is rounded independently instead.
edge_cases.outcome: Units of the last decimal place are lost or gained; the running-total technique is the same idea as the smooth distribution, applied where an ordering rather than a weight list is the natural input.

edge_cases.case: The tax is exigible on payment and the item's entry is not a cash basis entry.
edge_cases.outcome: The row's exigible indication is false, unless the entry is marked as always exigible; a tax return that shows only exigible lines filters on it.

worked_examples.description: The illustrating entry: every row with its allocated tax amount
worked_examples.narrative: The second tax item's total contribution is one thousand one hundred, so its two hundred twenty is split one thousand over one thousand one hundred, that is two hundred, and one hundred over one thousand one hundred, that is twenty. The fourth tax item's total is five thousand five hundred, so its two hundred seventy-five is split into one hundred, ten, one hundred fifty and fifteen. Every tax item's allocations add back exactly.

records.name: The tax identification number normalisation and check pipeline
records.purpose: Turns a number as typed into the stored, normalised form and decides whether it is accepted, refused or blanked, before any country routine is consulted.

operands.name: country
operands.source: the partner or the fiscal position carrying a foreign registration
operands.constraints: may be absent

operands.name: number as typed
operands.source: the user or an import
operands.constraints: may be empty or a single character

operands.name: label for the error message
operands.source: the caller, defaulting to the words for a value-added tax and replaced by the country's own label when the checked country is the acting company's country and that country defines one
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: validation mode
operands.source: the caller
operands.constraints: off, error, or blank on failure

preconditions.condition: A country and a number are both present.
preconditions.otherwise: The number is returned unchanged and no validated country is reported.

preconditions.condition: A number of a single character is the solidus, or the mode is off.
preconditions.otherwise: Under the blank-on-failure mode an empty number is returned; under the error mode the operation is refused with "To explicitly indicate no (valid) VAT, use '/' instead. ", whose trailing space is part of the message.

procedure: Return the number unchanged and report no validated country when there is no country or no number.
Handle a number of exactly one character: return it unchanged when it is a solidus or the mode is off, return an empty number under the blank-on-failure mode, and refuse under the error mode.

Split the prefix: the prefix is the first two characters uppercased when both are letters and empty otherwise; the remainder is everything after the first two characters with spaces removed, or the whole number when there is no prefix.

Return the number unchanged when the prefix is the two letters of the economic union itself and the country is not a member of that union, because a company outside the union that trades with non-businesses inside it may carry such a number.

Translate the prefix to a country code: the prefix used for Greece maps to the Greek country code and the prefix used for Northern Ireland maps to the United Kingdom country code; every other prefix is already the code.

When that country code belongs to the union-prefix country group and the stored country is itself in that group and a prefix was present, strip the prefix from the number and remember it as the prefixed country; otherwise remember that a second, union-wide attempt may be needed.
Take the code to check as the prefixed country when there is one and as the stored country's code otherwise.
Normalise the number with the country's formatting routine.
Replace the prefixed country by the Greek union prefix when it is the Greek country code.
Build the number to return as the prefixed country concatenated with the normalised number.
Return now when the mode is off or the caller asked for validation to be skipped.
Detect a doubled prefix: a prefixed country is present and the number to return starts with that prefix twice.

Run the country check on the normalised number; when it fails or the prefix is doubled, retry the whole pipeline against the country denoted by the prefix with the original prefixed number when a union-wide attempt is pending, refuse with the standard message under the error mode, and return an empty number under the blank-on-failure mode.
Return both the normalised number and the country code the number was validated for; the caller uses the second value to decide whether a fiscal position requiring a registration matches.
records.formula: prefix = the first two characters uppercased when both are letters , empty otherwise ; remainder = everything after the first two characters with spaces removed , or the whole number when there is no prefix ; code_to_check = the prefixed country when there is one , the stored country's code otherwise ; number_to_return = prefixed country concatenated with the normalised number ; doubled_prefix = a prefixed country is present and number_to_return starts with that prefix twice ; accepted = the country check succeeds and the prefix is not doubled , or the union-wide retry succeeds

rounding.what: Nothing; the pipeline manipulates text and whole numbers.
rounding.method: Every remainder used by a country check is the remainder of a Euclidean division whose result always carries the sign of the divisor, so minus three taken modulus eleven is eight.
rounding.step: Normalisation runs before the check, and the normalised form is what is stored.

result.name: the normalised number and the country code it was validated for
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the partner or on the fiscal position; the validated country decides whether a fiscal position requiring a registration matches.

edge_cases.case: No routine exists for the country.
edge_cases.outcome: The number is accepted unchanged.

edge_cases.case: The union-wide retry also fails.
edge_cases.outcome: The refusal is the standard message followed by a blank line and the sentence offering the European format, followed by the country's example number.

edge_cases.case: The record has no name, as for the anonymous storefront user, so its label contains the text naming a false value.
edge_cases.outcome: The shorter form of the standard message is used, without the words naming the record.

edge_cases.case: The country has no example.
edge_cases.outcome: The note giving the expected format is omitted from the message.

edge_cases.case: The number is imported as part of a file import.
edge_cases.outcome: The recomputation of the cross-border validity indication is cancelled, so importing ten thousand partners does not issue ten thousand requests.

worked_examples.description: A number typed with the Greek union prefix on a Greek partner
worked_examples.narrative: The two leading letters are the Greek union prefix, which translates to the Greek country code; the remainder is normalised, the prefixed country is put back as the union prefix rather than the country code, and the country check on the nine digits succeeds.

worked_examples.description: A number whose prefix is written twice
worked_examples.narrative: The number to return starts with the prefix twice, which is treated exactly like a failed country check: the union-wide retry is attempted when one is pending and the standard message is shown otherwise.

records.name: The weighted modulus primitive
records.purpose: The shape almost every country check is built on: a fixed list of weights paired with the digits of a number, summed, and reduced by a remainder.

operands.name: digits of the number
operands.source: the normalised number, read left to right unless the country says otherwise
operands.constraints: each is the position of the character in the stated alphabet, counted from zero

operands.name: weights
operands.source: the country's rule
operands.constraints: paired with the digits from the left unless stated otherwise; surplus digits are ignored when the weight list is shorter than the number

preconditions.condition: The number has at least as many digits as the weight list needs.
preconditions.otherwise: The country's own length test has already refused the number.

procedure: Pair each weight with the digit at the same position, from the left unless the country says the number is read from the right.
Multiply each pair and add the products.
Ignore the surplus digits when the weight list is shorter than the number.
Reduce the sum by the remainder the country's rule names.
records.formula: weighted_sum( number , weights ) = sum over i of ( weight_i × digit_i )

rounding.what: Nothing; the arithmetic is over whole numbers.
rounding.method: Every remainder is the remainder of a Euclidean division whose result carries the sign of the divisor, so minus three taken modulus eleven is eight.
rounding.step: The remainder is taken once, on the total.

result.name: the weighted sum
result.stored_or_displayed: Consumed by the country's check-digit rule; never stored.

edge_cases.case: The weight list is shorter than the number.
edge_cases.outcome: The surplus digits are ignored.

edge_cases.case: The country reads the number from the right.
edge_cases.outcome: The pairing starts at the last digit, which changes every product.

edge_cases.case: A weight is negative, as in the Polish rule.
edge_cases.outcome: The product is subtracted, which turns the usual comparison against a check digit into a test that the whole sum is a multiple of the divisor.

worked_examples.description: The weights of the Danish rule applied to its example number
worked_examples.narrative: Two plus fourteen plus eighteen plus twenty plus twenty plus eighteen plus fourteen plus four is one hundred ten, which is a multiple of eleven, so the Danish test passes.

records.name: The doubling checksum primitive
records.purpose: The alternating-doubling checksum several countries use, generalised to an alphabet of any size so that it can also run over letters.

operands.name: characters of the number
operands.source: the normalised number, read from right to left
operands.constraints: each value is the character's position in the alphabet, counted from zero

operands.name: alphabet size
operands.source: the country's rule
operands.constraints: ten for plain digits

preconditions.condition: Every character of the number belongs to the alphabet.
preconditions.otherwise: The country's own structural test has already refused the number.

procedure: Read the characters from right to left and take each one's position in the alphabet.
Add unchanged the value at every odd position, that is the first, the third, the fifth and each further position whose index is odd.

For each value at an even position, that is the second, the fourth, the sixth and each further position whose index is even, double it, take the whole part of the doubled value divided by the alphabet size, add the remainder of the doubled value by the alphabet size, and add that to the total.
Take the total modulus the alphabet size; the number is valid when the result is zero.

To produce a check character instead, append the alphabet's first character to the number, run the same checksum, and take the alphabet character at the position given by the alphabet size less that checksum, modulus the alphabet size.
records.formula: v1 … vm = the alphabet positions of the characters read RIGHT to LEFT ; checksum = ( sum of v at the odd positions 1, 3, 5, … + sum over v at the even positions 2, 4, 6, … of ( floor( v × 2 ÷ n ) + ( v × 2 mod n ) ) ) mod n ; valid when checksum = 0 ; check digit to append = alphabet[ ( n − checksum( number with alphabet[0] appended ) ) mod n ]

rounding.what: Nothing; the arithmetic is over whole numbers.
rounding.method: The whole part downwards for the division by the alphabet size, and a Euclidean remainder elsewhere.
rounding.step: The doubling and folding happen per character; the remainder is taken once, on the total.

result.name: the checksum, and the check character when one is being produced
result.unit_or_currency: a whole number or a character
result.stored_or_displayed: Consumed by the country's check; never stored on its own.

edge_cases.case: The alphabet is the plain digits.
edge_cases.outcome: The folding of the doubled value is the familiar rule of doubling the digit and adding the two resulting digits together.

edge_cases.case: The alphabet has thirty-six characters.
edge_cases.outcome: The same shape runs over digits and letters together.

edge_cases.case: A leading zero is significant.
edge_cases.outcome: The number must be padded before the checksum is taken, as the Israeli rule requires.

worked_examples.description: The Austrian example: the checksum of the seven digits before the check digit
worked_examples.narrative: The checksum of the seven digits is one, so the Austrian rule's check digit is six less one taken modulus ten, that is five, which is the last character of the quoted example.

worked_examples.description: A nine-digit number that is already valid
worked_examples.narrative: Reading from the right, the odd positions give nine and five and the even positions give nothing, so the checksum is four rather than zero and the number is not valid.

records.name: The recursive modulus eleven over ten primitive
records.purpose: A running check that folds each digit into a single carried value, used by three countries.

operands.name: digits of the number
operands.source: the normalised number, read left to right
operands.constraints: all digits

preconditions.condition: The country's length test has already succeeded.
preconditions.otherwise: The recursion would run over a number the country does not accept.

procedure: Start the carried value at five.
For each digit, left to right, read the carried value as ten when it is zero, double it, take the remainder by eleven, add the digit, and take the remainder by ten.
The number is valid when the carried value is one after the last digit.
To produce a check digit instead, take one less twice the carried value taken modulus eleven, again reading a carried value of zero as ten, and take the remainder by ten.
records.formula: check = 5 ; for each digit d , left to right : check = ( ( ( check , or 10 when check is 0 ) × 2 ) mod 11 + d ) mod 10 ; valid when check = 1 ; check digit to append = ( 1 − ( ( check , or 10 when check is 0 ) × 2 ) mod 11 ) mod 10

rounding.what: Nothing; the arithmetic is over whole numbers.
rounding.method: Euclidean remainders, whose result carries the sign of the divisor.
rounding.step: Two remainders per digit, taken in the stated order.

result.name: the carried value, and the check digit when one is being produced
result.stored_or_displayed: Consumed by the country's check.

edge_cases.case: The carried value reaches zero.
edge_cases.outcome: It is read as ten before being doubled; an implementation that doubles zero produces a different result from the second digit onwards.

edge_cases.case: The check digit is included in the walk.
edge_cases.outcome: The final carried value is one for a valid number, which is why the walk covers every digit and not only the body.

worked_examples.description: The German example number, nine digits
worked_examples.narrative: Starting at five: twice five is ten, ten taken modulus eleven is ten, plus one is eleven, modulus ten is one. Twice one is two, plus two is four. Twice four is eight, plus three is eleven, modulus ten is one. Twice one is two, plus four is six. Twice six is twelve, modulus eleven is one, plus five is six. Twice six is twelve, modulus eleven is one, plus six is seven. Twice seven is fourteen, modulus eleven is three, plus seven is ten, modulus ten is zero. The zero is read as ten, twice ten is twenty, modulus eleven is nine, plus eight is seventeen, modulus ten is seven. Twice seven is fourteen, modulus eleven is three, plus eight is eleven, modulus ten is one: the final value is one, so the number is valid.

records.name: The recursive modulus thirty-seven over thirty-six primitive
records.purpose: The same running shape over an alphabet of thirty-six characters, so that a number containing letters can carry a check.

operands.name: characters of the number
operands.source: the normalised number, read left to right
operands.constraints: the alphabet is the ten digits followed by the twenty-six letters

preconditions.condition: Every character belongs to the thirty-six-character alphabet.
preconditions.otherwise: The country's structural test has already refused the number.

procedure: Start the carried value at eighteen.

For each character, left to right, read the carried value as thirty-six when it is zero, double it, take the remainder by thirty-seven, add the character's position in the alphabet, and take the remainder by thirty-six.
The number is valid when the carried value is one after the last character.
records.formula: check = 18 ; for each character c , left to right : check = ( ( ( check , or 36 when check is 0 ) × 2 ) mod 37 + value(c) ) mod 36 ; valid when check = 1
